docs.title: Question
docs.text: What do Jude 6-7 actually teach about the angels' sin? Specifically: 1. What does "kept not their first estate, left their own habitation" mean? 2. What does "in like manner" (ton homoion tropon) connect? 3. What is "strange flesh" (heteras sarkos)? 4. Does this passage support the Genesis 6 angel interpretation?

docs.title: The Passage
docs.text: Jude 6: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Jude 7: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

docs.title: Methodological Approach
docs.text: Following proper hermeneutics: 1. Examine what the text ACTUALLY STATES 2. Use Scripture to interpret Scripture (especially Rev 12, per 2 Peter 2:4 study) 3. Analyze the Greek grammar carefully 4. Avoid importing extra-biblical sources (1 Enoch) as authoritative 5. Let context determine meaning

docs.title: Key Interpretive Parallel: Revelation 12
docs.text:
From the 2 Peter 2:4 study, we established that Revelation 12 describes fallen angels: - "Cast out" of heaven (Rev 12:9) - "Neither was their place found any more in heaven" (Rev 12:8) - Yet remain ACTIVE on earth (Rev 12:12-17)

This provides a biblical framework for understanding Jude 6: - "Kept not their first estate" → lost their position in heaven - "Left their own habitation" → cast out of heaven to earth - "Reserved... unto judgment" → "knoweth he hath but a short time"

docs.title: ANGEL Topic
docs.text: Key entries: - "Of different orders" - ISA 6:2; 1TH 4:16; 1PE 3:22; Jude 1:9; REV 12:7 - "Do not marry" - MAT 22:30; MRK 12:25; LUK 20:35 - "Are obedient" - PSA 103:20; MAT 6:10; Jude 1:6 - "FALLEN" - (category exists but details sparse)

docs.title: SODOM Topic
docs.text: Key entries: - Wickedness of inhabitants - GEN 13:13; 19:4-13; Jude 1:7 - Destroyed on account of wickedness - GEN 19:1-29; 2PE 2:6

docs.title: SODOMY / SODOMITES Topics
docs.text:
• "Inhabitants of Sodom, many of whom openly practiced homosexuality"
  • GEN 19:4-14; ROM 1:24,26,27; 1CO 6:9

docs.title: 1. What does "kept not their first estate" mean?
docs.text:
• Greek: arche (G746) = beginning, origin, principality, domain
  • Does this refer to leaving angelic nature, or leaving position/rank?

docs.title: 2. What does "left their own habitation" mean?
docs.text:
• Greek: oiketerion (G3613) = dwelling place
  • Only used twice: Jude 6 and 2 Cor 5:2 (heavenly body)
  • Does this mean leaving heaven, or leaving angelic form?

docs.title: 3. What does "in like manner" connect?
docs.text:
• Greek: ton homoion tropon
  • Does it connect Sodom's sin TO the angels' sin?
  • Or connect the surrounding cities TO Sodom?
  • Or describe the manner of judgment?

docs.title: 4. What is "strange flesh"?
docs.text:
• Greek: heteras sarkos = different/other flesh
  • Sodom's sin was homosexuality (same sex) - how is that "different" flesh?
  • Or does this refer to the angels in Genesis 19 (different species)?

docs.title: 2 Peter 2:4 Study - Key Findings
docs.text:
• "Cast down" and "chains of darkness" describe spiritual state, not physical prison
  • Revelation 12 shows "cast down" angels who remain active
  • No need for "two classes" of fallen angels theory
  • Genesis 6 connection is not required - Rev 12 provides simpler explanation

docs.title: 1 Peter 3:19-20 Study - Key Findings
docs.text:
• "Spirits in prison" were HUMANS who rejected Noah's preaching
  • Different vocabulary: "spirits" (pneuma) vs "angels" (aggelos)
  • Should not be conflated with fallen angels passages

docs.title: Fate of the Wicked Study - Key Findings
docs.text:
• "Eternal fire" results in destruction, not eternal conscious torment
  • Sodom's fire has ceased but the destruction is permanent
  • Same fate awaits Satan and his angels

docs.title: The Primary Passage: Jude 5-8
docs.text: Jude 5: I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. Jude 6: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Jude 7: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. Jude 8: Likewise also these [filthy] dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.

docs.title: The Purpose: Warning Against False Teachers (vv. 3-4)
docs.text: Jude 3: ...it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort [you] that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. Jude 4: For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

docs.title: Three Examples of Judgment (vv. 5-7)
docs.text:
1. Israel in the wilderness (v.5) - "destroyed them that believed not"
  2. Angels (v.6) - "reserved in everlasting chains under darkness"
  3. Sodom and Gomorrah (v.7) - "suffering the vengeance of eternal fire"

docs.title: Application to False Teachers (vv. 8-16)
docs.text: Jude 8: Likewise also these [filthy] dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities. Jude 11: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. Jude 13: ...wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.

docs.title: The Key Interpretive Parallel: Revelation 12:7-12
docs.text:
Rev 12:7: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, Rev 12:8: And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. Rev 12:9: And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him. Rev 12:10: ...for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. Rev 12:12: ...for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.

Connection to Jude 6: | Jude 6 | Revelation 12 | |--------|---------------| | "kept not their first estate" | "neither was their place found any more in heaven" | | "left their own habitation" | "cast out into the earth" | | "reserved... unto judgment" | "knoweth he hath but a short time" |

docs.title: Parallel Passage: 2 Peter 2:4-6
docs.text:
2 Peter 2:4: For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast [them] down to hell, and delivered [them] into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; 2 Peter 2:5: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth [person], a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; 2 Peter 2:6: And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned [them] with an overthrow, making [them] an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;

Note: Peter and Jude both use angels and Sodom as examples. Peter adds Noah/flood; Jude adds Israel in wilderness.

docs.title: The Sodom Account: Genesis 19:1-13
docs.text:
Gen 19:1: And there came two angels to Sodom at even... Gen 19:4-5: But before they lay down, the men of the city, [even] the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter: And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where [are] the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them. Gen 19:7: And said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. Gen 19:8: Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you... Gen 19:13: For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxen great before the face of the LORD... Gen 19:24-25: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven; And he overthrew those cities...

Key observation: The men of Sodom wanted to "know" the angels (male visitors). This was homosexual assault - men pursuing men, not humans pursuing angels for their angelic nature.

docs.title: Angels and Marriage: Jesus's Teaching
docs.text:
Matthew 22:30: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.

Mark 12:25: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven.

Luke 20:35-36: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.

Key observation: Jesus says angels in heaven do not marry. This is relevant to whether angels could/would take human wives.

docs.title: Jude's Quotation of Enoch (vv. 14-15)
docs.text:
Jude 14-15: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all...

Note: Jude quotes material attributed to Enoch. This appears in 1 Enoch 1:9. However: - Quoting something doesn't endorse the entire source - Paul quoted pagan poets (Acts 17:28; Titus 1:12) without endorsing paganism - The question is what SCRIPTURE teaches, not what 1 Enoch says

docs.title: Other References to Sodom's Sin
docs.text:
Ezekiel 16:49-50: Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw [good].

Isaiah 3:9: The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide [it] not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.

Romans 1:26-27: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly...

Key observation: Scripture consistently identifies Sodom's sin as sexual immorality between humans, particularly homosexuality - not as humans pursuing angels.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text: This analysis will: 1. Examine what Jude actually states 2. Use Revelation 12 as the primary interpretive parallel (per 2 Peter 2:4 study) 3. Carefully analyze the Greek grammar of "in like manner" 4. Address the "strange flesh" question 5. Evaluate the Genesis 6 connection

docs.title: The Purpose
docs.text: Jude writes to warn about false teachers who have "crept in unawares" (v.4). His argument: God has judged such rebels before, and will again.

docs.title: Three Examples of Judgment (vv. 5-7)
docs.text: Example Sin Judgment Israel in wilderness Unbelief "destroyed them that believed not" Angels "kept not... left" "reserved in everlasting chains" Sodom & Gomorrah Fornication, strange flesh "suffering the vengeance of eternal fire"

docs.title: The Application (v.8)
docs.text:
"Likewise also these [filthy] dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities."

The false teachers follow the pattern of all three examples.

docs.title: Analysis of Jude 6: The Angels' Sin
The Text
docs.text: "And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day."

docs.title: Key Phrase 1: "Kept not their first estate"
docs.text:
Greek: τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴν (ten heauton archen) - arche (G746) = beginning, origin, principality, rule, domain

Meaning options: 1. Did not keep their original position/rank 2. Did not keep their proper domain/sphere of authority 3. Did not keep their original nature

Revelation 12 parallel:

"And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven" (Rev 12:8)

The angels lost their POSITION in heaven through rebellion. This matches "kept not their first estate" - they abandoned their proper rank/domain by following Satan.

docs.title: Key Phrase 2: "Left their own habitation"
docs.text:
Greek: ἀπολιπόντας τὸ ἴδιον οἰκητήριον (apolipontas to idion oiketerion) - oiketerion (G3613) = dwelling place, habitation

Usage: Only appears twice in NT: 1. Jude 6 - angels left their "habitation" 2. 2 Cor 5:2 - believers groan for our heavenly "habitation" (body)

Common interpretation: Because oiketerion refers to a body in 2 Cor 5:2, angels left their "angelic body" to take human form.

Problem with this interpretation: 1. Context determines meaning - the contexts are very different 2. 2 Cor 5:2 is about resurrection bodies; Jude 6 is about rebellion 3. This requires importing 2 Cor 5:2's meaning into Jude 6

Revelation 12 parallel:

"he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him" (Rev 12:9)

The angels left heaven - their proper dwelling place. They were cast out to earth. This matches "left their own habitation" without requiring a change of bodily form.

docs.title: Key Phrase 3: "Reserved in everlasting chains under darkness"
docs.text:
From 2 Peter 2:4 study: - "Chains of darkness" describes spiritual state, not physical prison - Revelation 12 shows "cast down" angels who remain ACTIVE - "Reserved unto judgment" = "knoweth he hath but a short time"

The angels are spiritually condemned (in darkness, bound to judgment) but not necessarily inactive.

docs.title: Summary of Jude 6
docs.text: Jude 6, interpreted through Revelation 12, describes: 1. Angels who rebelled with Satan 2. They abandoned their proper position/rank in heaven 3. They were cast out of their heavenly dwelling 4. They are spiritually condemned, awaiting judgment 5. No reference to Genesis 6 or taking human wives

docs.title: Analysis of Jude 7: "In Like Manner" and "Strange Flesh"
The Text
docs.text: "Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire."

docs.title: The Critical Question: What Does "In Like Manner" Connect?
docs.text:
Greek: τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον τούτοις (ton homoion tropon toutois) - "in like manner to these"

Three possible readings:

docs.title: Option A: Sodom sinned like the angels (sexual sin connection)
docs.text:
Reading: "Sodom, in like manner [as the angels], giving themselves to fornication..."

This would mean: - The angels committed sexual sin - Sodom committed similar sexual sin - Both went after "strange flesh"

Problems: 1. The grammar doesn't clearly support this 2. "toutois" (these) is ambiguous - what does it refer to? 3. This requires assuming the angels' sin was sexual (not stated in Jude 6)

docs.title: Option B: The surrounding cities sinned like Sodom
docs.text:
Reading: "Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities about them in like manner..."

This would mean: - The surrounding cities sinned in the same manner as Sodom - All engaged in fornication and strange flesh

Support: 1. Grammatically natural - "the cities about them in like manner" 2. "toutois" refers to Sodom and Gomorrah 3. Doesn't require assuming the angels' sin

docs.title: Option C: All three examples illustrate judgment "in like manner"
docs.text:
Reading: All three examples (Israel, angels, Sodom) show God judging sin in a similar pattern.

Support: 1. Jude's point is about God's judgment pattern 2. V.8 says "Likewise also these dreamers" - connecting to all three

docs.title: Grammatical Analysis
docs.text:
The phrase τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον τούτοις most naturally modifies "the cities about them":

"Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities about them [sinning] in like manner [to them]..."

The surrounding cities (Admah, Zeboim - Deut 29:23) committed the same sins as Sodom and Gomorrah. This is the most straightforward grammatical reading.

docs.title: What Is "Strange Flesh" (heteras sarkos)?
docs.text:
Greek: σαρκὸς ἑτέρας (sarkos heteras) - heteros (G2087) = other, different, another of a different kind - sarx (G4561) = flesh

The interpretive question: What makes the flesh "different/strange"?

docs.title: Option A: Humans pursuing angelic flesh (cross-species)
docs.text:
If Sodom's sin was pursuing the angels (Gen 19), "different flesh" = angelic vs human.

Problems: 1. Genesis 19 shows the men of Sodom didn't know the visitors were angels 2. They wanted to "know" what appeared to be MEN 3. Lot offered his daughters as substitutes - suggesting the desire was sexual, not angel-specific 4. The men refused the daughters - their sin was homosexuality, not angel-pursuit

docs.title: Option B: Men pursuing male flesh (homosexuality)
docs.text:
"Strange/different flesh" = pursuing the same sex instead of the opposite sex.

Support: 1. Genesis 19:4-5 - men wanted the male visitors 2. Genesis 19:8 - Lot offered daughters, men refused 3. Romans 1:26-27 - describes homosexuality as "against nature" 4. The word "heteros" means "different" - men pursuing men is pursuing flesh "different" from the natural (female)

Key insight: From the perspective of natural sexuality, men pursuing men IS pursuing "different/other" flesh - flesh that is not the natural counterpart (female).

docs.title: Option C: Connection to Genesis 6 angels taking wives
docs.text:
If the angels in Jude 6 = angels of Genesis 6, and if "in like manner" connects to them, then "strange flesh" might mean angels pursuing human flesh.

Problems: 1. Requires multiple assumptions 2. Jude 6 doesn't mention Genesis 6 3. The "in like manner" grammar doesn't clearly support this 4. Reverses the direction - in Gen 19, humans pursued angels, not angels pursuing humans

docs.title: The Question of Jude Quoting 1 Enoch
The Fact
docs.text: Jude 14-15 quotes material that appears in 1 Enoch 1:9.

docs.title: Does This Endorse 1 Enoch's Theology?
docs.text:
No, for these reasons:

  1. Quoting doesn't equal endorsing the entire source
  2. Paul quoted pagan poets (Acts 17:28; Titus 1:12)

  3. This doesn't mean Paul endorsed Greek paganism

  4. Jude may be quoting oral tradition, not the book

  5. Enoch was a historical person (Gen 5:21-24)

  6. A genuine prophecy could exist independently of the book

  7. Scripture is the authority, not 1 Enoch

  8. 1 Enoch elaborates extensively on angel-human marriages
  9. But Jude does NOT include these details

  10. If Jude wanted to teach the 1 Enoch angel view, why not include those details?

  11. Jude's description fits Revelation 12

  12. "kept not their first estate" = lost their position
  13. "left their own habitation" = cast out of heaven
  14. No need to import 1 Enoch's interpretation

docs.title: Does Jude Support the Genesis 6 Angel Interpretation?
The Argument For
docs.text:
1. Jude mentions angels (v.6) then Sodom (v.7)
  2. "In like manner" connects them
  3. "Strange flesh" implies cross-species sin
  4. Jude quotes 1 Enoch (vv.14-15)

docs.title: The Problems
docs.text:
1. Jude 6 doesn't describe sexual sin
  2. "Kept not their first estate, left their own habitation" describes rebellion/departure
  3. Revelation 12 explains this as the war in heaven

  4. No mention of taking wives or producing offspring

  5. "In like manner" grammar

  6. Most naturally connects to "the cities about them"

  7. Not clearly connecting Sodom's sin to the angels' sin

  8. "Strange flesh" in context

  9. Genesis 19 shows homosexual assault, not angel-pursuit
  10. The men didn't know the visitors were angels

  11. "Different flesh" = same-sex pursuit

  12. Peter's parallel doesn't support it

  13. 2 Peter 2:4 simply says "angels that sinned"
  14. No description of sexual sin
  15. Peter adds Noah/flood BETWEEN angels and Sodom
  16. Jude adds Israel BEFORE angels

  17. Neither author structures the list to connect angels directly to Genesis 6

  18. Jesus's teaching about angels

  19. "Angels in heaven neither marry nor are given in marriage" (Matt 22:30)
  20. This suggests angels don't have sexual function

docs.title: Honest Assessment: What Jude Actually Says
Jude 6 States:
docs.text:
1. Angels did not keep their proper position
  2. Angels left their proper dwelling
  3. They are reserved for judgment

docs.title: Jude 6 Does NOT State:
docs.text:
1. WHEN they sinned
  2. That their sin was sexual
  3. That they took human wives
  4. That this is the Genesis 6 event
  5. Any connection to Nephilim

docs.title: Jude 7 States:
docs.text:
1. Sodom and the surrounding cities committed fornication
  2. They went after "strange flesh"
  3. They suffered eternal fire as an example

docs.title: The "In Like Manner" Question:
docs.text:
The grammar most naturally reads: "Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities about them [sinning] in like manner [to Sodom]..."

Even if "in like manner" connects to the angels, it would only mean Sodom's judgment was similar to the angels' judgment - not that their sins were identical.

docs.title: Conclusion of Analysis
docs.text:
Jude 6-7, properly analyzed:

  1. The angels' sin (v.6) is rebellion - abandoning their position and being cast out of heaven. This matches Revelation 12, not Genesis 6.

  2. "In like manner" (v.7) most naturally connects "the cities about them" to Sodom, not Sodom to the angels.

  3. "Strange flesh" (v.7) refers to Sodom's homosexuality - men pursuing men instead of the natural counterpart. The men of Sodom didn't know the visitors were angels.

  4. Jude's purpose is to warn about judgment, not to teach angel chronology. He gives three examples of God judging sin, not a connected narrative about angel-human interbreeding.

  5. The 1 Enoch quotation (vv.14-15) doesn't endorse 1 Enoch's entire theology, just as Paul's quotation of pagan poets didn't endorse paganism.

The Genesis 6 connection is not required by Jude 6-7 and introduces assumptions not present in the text.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Greek: ἀρχή (arche) Strong's G746: beginning, origin, first place, principality, rule, magistracy

docs.title: Meanings
docs.text:
1. Beginning/Origin - the starting point (John 1:1 "In the beginning")
  2. Leadership/Rule - authority, principality, dominion
  3. Proper Position/Rank - one's assigned place in an order

docs.title: Usage in Scripture (58 occurrences)
docs.text:
Most commonly translated: - "beginning" (40x) - "principality" (8x) - "rule" (2x)

Key passages about spiritual powers: - Eph 1:21 - "Far above all principality (arche), and power..." - Col 1:16 - "...whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities (arche)..." - Rom 8:38 - "nor principalities (arche), nor powers..."

docs.title: Meaning in Jude 6
docs.text:
"The angels which kept not their first estate (arche)..."

The angels did not maintain their proper position, rank, or domain in the cosmic order. They abandoned their assigned place.

Revelation 12 parallel: "neither was their place found any more in heaven" (Rev 12:8)

The term refers to their position/rank, not their physical nature or form.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Greek: οἰκητήριον (oiketerion) Strong's G3613: a residence, dwelling place, habitation

docs.title: Etymology
docs.text: From oikeo (G3611) = "to dwell"

docs.title: All NT Occurrences (Only 2)
docs.text:
1. 2 Corinthians 5:2: "For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house (oiketerion) which is from heaven."

  2. Context: The resurrection body believers will receive

  3. Jude 6: "the angels which... left their own habitation (oiketerion)"

  4. Context: Angels who rebelled

docs.title: Interpretive Question
docs.text:
Some argue: Since oiketerion means "body" in 2 Cor 5:2, it means "body" in Jude 6 too. Therefore, angels left their "angelic bodies" to take human form.

Problems with this reasoning:

  1. Context determines meaning - 2 Cor 5 is about resurrection bodies; Jude 6 is about rebellion
  2. The word means "dwelling place" - in 2 Cor 5:2, the body IS the dwelling place of the spirit
  3. In Jude 6, the dwelling could be heaven itself - where angels properly dwell

docs.title: Better Interpretation
docs.text:
"Left their own habitation" = left their proper dwelling place (heaven)

Revelation 12 parallel: "he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him" (Rev 12:9)

The angels left heaven - they were cast out. This is their "habitation" that they left.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Greek: ἕτερος (heteros) Strong's G2087: the other, another, different

docs.title: Nuance
docs.text:
Heteros indicates something "other" or "different" - often with a sense of qualitative difference, not just numerical distinction.

Compare with allos (G243) which means "another" without emphasizing difference.

docs.title: Usage (99 occurrences)
docs.text:
• "another" (43x)
  • "other" (42x)
  • "strange" (2x)

docs.title: In Jude 7: "Strange Flesh" (sarkos heteras)
docs.text:
"going after strange flesh (sarkos heteras)"

Literally: "different flesh" or "other flesh"

docs.title: What Makes It "Different"?
docs.text:
Option A: Angelic flesh (different species) If Sodom pursued angels, the flesh would be "different" = non-human.

Problems: - Genesis 19 shows the men didn't know visitors were angels - They appeared as men - Lot offered daughters as substitute - suggesting sexual desire, not angel-pursuit

Option B: Same-sex flesh (different from natural) Men pursuing men = pursuing flesh "different" from the natural female counterpart.

Support: - Romans 1:26-27 describes homosexuality as "against nature" - The natural counterpart for a man is a woman - Pursuing men is pursuing "heteros" (different/other) flesh from God's design - Genesis 19:4-5 clearly shows men demanding male visitors - Genesis 19:8 - men refused female substitutes

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
"Strange flesh" (heteras sarkos) = "different/other flesh" = pursuing the same sex instead of the natural opposite sex.

The men of Sodom pursued flesh that was "different" from God's design - male instead of female.

docs.title: Key Phrase: "In Like Manner" (ton homoion tropon)
Greek
docs.text: τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον τούτοις (ton homoion tropon toutois) - "in like/similar manner to these"

docs.title: Grammatical Question
docs.text:
What does "toutois" (these) refer to?

Option A: The angels (v.6) - Sodom sinned like the angels Option B: Sodom and Gomorrah - the surrounding cities sinned like Sodom Option C: All the examples - the manner of judgment is similar

docs.title: Most Natural Reading
docs.text:
"Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities about them in like manner [to them]..."

The phrase "the cities about them" is immediately followed by "in like manner." This most naturally means the surrounding cities (Admah, Zeboim - Deut 29:23) committed the same sins as Sodom.

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text:
If "in like manner" connects to the angels, it would suggest Sodom's sin was similar to the angels' sin - supporting the sexual interpretation.

But if "in like manner" connects to "the cities about them," it simply means the whole region committed the same sins - no connection to the angels' sin is implied.

The grammar favors Option B.

docs.title: Summary of Word Studies
docs.text: Term Greek Meaning Application First estate arche (G746) Position, rank, domain Angels lost their proper position in heaven Habitation oiketerion (G3613) Dwelling place Angels left heaven (their proper dwelling) Strange heteros (G2087) Other, different Sodom pursued "different" flesh (same-sex) In like manner ton homoion tropon In similar fashion The surrounding cities sinned like Sodom

docs.title: What Word Studies Do NOT Support
docs.text:
1. Angels taking on physical bodies (oiketerion doesn't require this)
  2. Angels committing sexual sin (arche refers to position, not nature)
  3. "In like manner" connecting Sodom's sin to the angels' sin (grammar favors connecting to surrounding cities)
  4. Sodom pursuing angels as angels (heteros more naturally refers to same-sex pursuit)

docs.title: Conclusion: Jude 6-7 - The Angels' Sin and Sodom's Sin
Question 1: What does "kept not their first estate, left their own habitation" mean?
docs.text:
Answer: The angels abandoned their proper position (arche = rank/domain) and left their dwelling place (oiketerion = heaven).

Evidence: - Arche (G746) means position, principality, domain - not physical nature - Oiketerion (G3613) means dwelling place - in context, heaven - Revelation 12:8-9 provides the biblical parallel: "neither was their place found any more in heaven... cast out into the earth"

Conclusion: Jude 6 describes the angelic rebellion - following Satan, losing their position in heaven, being cast out. This is NOT a description of angels taking human form or marrying women.

docs.title: Question 2: What does "in like manner" (ton homoion tropon) connect?
docs.text:
Answer: Most naturally, it connects "the cities about them" to Sodom and Gomorrah.

The Reading:

"Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities about them in like manner [to them], giving themselves over to fornication..."

Evidence: - The phrase immediately follows "the cities about them" - The surrounding cities (Admah, Zeboim - Deut 29:23) were destroyed for the same sins - This reading doesn't require assuming the angels' sin was sexual

Alternative readings (connecting to angels or to judgment pattern) are grammatically possible but less natural.

docs.title: Question 3: What is "strange flesh" (heteras sarkos)?
docs.text:
Answer: "Different/other flesh" refers to homosexuality - men pursuing men instead of the natural female counterpart.

Evidence: - Heteros (G2087) = other, different (qualitatively) - Genesis 19:4-5 shows men demanding male visitors - Genesis 19:8 shows men refusing female substitutes - their desire was specifically homosexual - Romans 1:26-27 describes homosexuality as "against nature" - The men of Sodom didn't know the visitors were angels - they appeared as men

Key insight: From God's design perspective, men pursuing men IS pursuing "different" flesh - flesh that is not the natural counterpart.

docs.title: Question 4: Does this passage support the Genesis 6 angel interpretation?
docs.text:
Answer: No. Jude 6-7 does NOT require or clearly support the Genesis 6 angel interpretation.

What Jude 6 actually says: - Angels abandoned their position and dwelling (rebellion) - They are reserved for judgment

What Jude 6 does NOT say: - That they took human wives - That they produced offspring - That this was the Genesis 6 event - Any reference to Nephilim

What Jude 7 actually says: - Sodom committed fornication - Sodom pursued "strange flesh" (homosexuality)

What Jude 7 does NOT say: - That Sodom's sin was identical to the angels' sin - That "strange flesh" means angelic flesh

docs.title: 2 Peter 2:4 Study - Consistent Findings
docs.text: 2 Peter 2:4 Study Jude 6-7 Study "Cast down" = expelled from heaven "Left their habitation" = same "Chains of darkness" = spiritual state "Everlasting chains under darkness" = same Revelation 12 is the interpretive key Revelation 12 explains the rebellion No Genesis 6 connection required No Genesis 6 connection required

docs.title: 1 Peter 3:19-20 Study - Different Subject
docs.text: 1 Peter 3:19-20 Jude 6 "Spirits" (pneuma) "Angels" (aggelos) Human spirits who rejected Noah Angels who rebelled with Satan Different vocabulary Different vocabulary Should NOT be conflated Should NOT be conflated

docs.title: Fate of the Wicked Study - Consistent on "Eternal Fire"
docs.text:
Jude 7: "suffering the vengeance of eternal fire"

This is consistent with the fate-of-the-wicked conclusion: - "Eternal fire" describes the RESULT, not endless burning - Sodom's fire has ceased, but the destruction is permanent - Same fate awaits the wicked and fallen angels

docs.title: Jude's Purpose
docs.text: To warn about false teachers who have "crept in unawares" (v.4).

docs.title: Jude's Method
docs.text: Three examples of God judging rebels: 1. Israel - unbelief → destroyed 2. Angels - rebellion → reserved for judgment 3. Sodom - sexual sin → destroyed by fire

docs.title: Jude's Application (v.8)
docs.text:
"Likewise also these [filthy] dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities."

The false teachers combine elements of all three examples: - Like Israel: they are among God's people but rebel - Like the angels: they "despise dominion" (reject authority) - Like Sodom: they "defile the flesh" (sexual sin)

Jude is NOT teaching a connected narrative about angel-human interbreeding. He is giving three examples of rebellion and judgment.

docs.title: Final Answer: The Angels' Sin
docs.text:
Based on Jude 6-7 interpreted through Scripture (especially Revelation 12):

  1. The sin: Rebellion against God - joining Satan's war in heaven
  2. The result: Cast out of heaven, position lost
  3. The current state: Spiritually condemned ("chains of darkness"), awaiting judgment
  4. The connection to Sodom: Both are examples of God judging sin - NOT that they committed the same sin

The Genesis 6 connection is NOT established by Jude 6-7. This passage describes the angelic rebellion (Rev 12), not a separate event of angels taking human wives.

docs.title: Implications for Genesis 6 Study
docs.text:
This study does NOT answer the Genesis 6 question. It only establishes that Jude 6-7 cannot be used as decisive evidence for the angel interpretation.

What Jude 6-7 tells us: - Angels rebelled and were judged - Sodom committed sexual sin and was judged - God judges sin

What Jude 6-7 does NOT tell us: - That "sons of God" in Genesis 6 were angels - That angels can or did take human wives - That Nephilim were angel-human offspring

These questions must be answered from other texts: - Genesis 6 itself (immediate context) - "Sons of God" usage survey - Jesus's teaching on angels and marriage (Matt 22:30) - Nephilim word study

docs.title: Summary Table
docs.text: Question Answer What is the angels' sin (Jude 6)? Rebellion - abandoning position, cast from heaven What does "in like manner" connect? Most likely: surrounding cities to Sodom What is "strange flesh"? Homosexuality - men pursuing men Does Jude support Genesis 6 angels? No - text doesn't require this interpretation Is Jude 6 = 2 Peter 2:4? Yes - same event described Is Jude 6 = Revelation 12? Yes - the angelic rebellion Is Jude 6 = Genesis 6? Not established - requires assumptions beyond text

docs.title: Question
docs.text: What did Jesus mean by "as the days of Noah" in Matthew 24:37? Was he referring to angels mixing with humans (Genesis 6 "sons of God"), or something else entirely?

docs.title: ANTEDILUVIANS
docs.text:
Nave's specifically connects Matthew 24:37-39 and Luke 17:26,27 to the antediluvian (pre-flood) period:

-Wickedness of GEN 6:5-7
-Destruction of GEN 7:1,21-23; JOB 22:15-17; MAT 24:37-39; LUK 17:26,27; 2PE 2:5

Key observation: Nave's connects Jesus's reference to the destruction of the antediluvians, not to the "sons of God" passage specifically.

docs.title: NOAH
docs.text: -His life preserved at the time of the great flood GEN 6:18; 7:8; MAT 24:38; HEB 11:7; 1PE 3:20

docs.title: FLOOD
docs.text: The flood narrative is the primary context for Jesus's reference.

docs.title: genesis-6-sons-of-god (CONCLUSION.md)
docs.text: Key findings from this study: - The Sethite view (godly line of Seth) appears better supported than the angel view - Genesis 6:3 calls the "sons of God" flesh - human terminology - Jesus teaches angels do not marry (Matt 22:30) - Moses never uses "bene elohim" for angels elsewhere

docs.title: Key Quote from the Study:
docs.text: "God's response treats the 'sons of God' as 'flesh' and focuses on human judgment"

docs.title: The Core Issue
docs.text:
When Jesus said "as the days of Noah," what did HE choose to emphasize?

Option A: The supernatural element - angel-human mixing, Nephilim, corruption of bloodlines Option B: The ordinary element - normal life activities, unawareness, sudden judgment

This study will examine Jesus's own words to determine His intended meaning.

docs.title: Preliminary Observations
docs.text:
Looking at the texts:

Matthew 24:38 - Jesus emphasizes: - "eating and drinking" - "marrying and giving in marriage" - "until the day that Noe entered into the ark" - "knew not"

Luke 17:27-28 - Jesus emphasizes: - "They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage" - Then parallels with Lot: "they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded"

Notable omissions from Jesus's description: - No mention of "sons of God" - No mention of "daughters of men" - No mention of Nephilim/giants - No mention of angels - No mention of supernatural mixing - No mention of corruption of flesh

Jesus chose to emphasize ordinary activities and unawareness, not supernatural corruption.

1. People were living ordinary lives - eating, drinking, marrying

docs.title: The Lot Parallel (Luke 17:28-29)
docs.text:
Jesus parallels Noah's days with Lot's days. In Lot's case: - They were "eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building" - Destruction came the day Lot left - Fire destroyed them all

Critical point: The Lot parallel proves Jesus's point was about ordinary life interrupted by sudden judgment, NOT about any supernatural element unique to Noah's time.

docs.title: The Central Question
docs.text:
What did Jesus mean by "as the days of Noah" (Matthew 24:37)? Two primary interpretations exist:

View What Jesus Referenced Supernatural View The "sons of God"/angel mixing with humans, Nephilim, supernatural corruption Ordinary Life View Normal daily activities, spiritual unawareness, sudden unexpected judgment

This analysis will examine Jesus's own words to determine which view He intended.

docs.title: Exegetical Analysis: What Did Jesus Actually Say?
Matthew 24:37-39 - Jesus's Full Explanation
docs.text:
v.37: "But as the days of Noe [were], so shall also the coming of the Son of man be."

v.38: "For [γάρ/gar - explanatory] as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,"

v.39: "And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be."

Critical observation: Jesus provided His own interpretation.

The word "For" (γάρ/gar) in v.38 is explanatory - Jesus is explaining what He means by "days of Noah." His explanation consists of:

  1. Eating and drinking - Normal sustenance activities
  2. Marrying and giving in marriage - Normal social/family activities
  3. Knew not - Unawareness/unconcern
  4. Until the day - Sudden, unexpected timing
  5. Took them all away - Complete, inescapable judgment

Jesus did NOT explain "days of Noah" by referencing: - Sons of God - Daughters of men - Nephilim/giants - Angels - Supernatural mixing - Corruption of bloodlines - Unusual wickedness

docs.title: The Explanatory Power of γάρ (gar)
docs.text: When Jesus says "as the days of Noah... for they were eating and drinking," the conjunction γάρ introduces His authoritative explanation of what "days of Noah" means for His teaching. Whatever else may have characterized Noah's days, Jesus selected these elements as relevant to His point.

docs.title: The Luke 17 Parallel: Lot Confirms the Interpretation
Luke 17:26-30
docs.text:
v.26: "And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man."

v.27: "They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all."

v.28: "Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;"

v.29: "But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed [them] all."

v.30: "Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed."

docs.title: The Lot Parallel as Interpretive Key
docs.text:
Jesus draws an explicit parallel between Noah's days and Lot's days:

Noah's Days Lot's Days Eating, drinking Eating, drinking Marrying Buying, selling - Planting, building Sudden flood Sudden fire Destroyed all Destroyed all

Critical observation: Lot's days had NO "sons of God" element, NO Nephilim, NO angel-human mixing. Yet Jesus says "Likewise" (ὁμοίως/homoios) - in the same way.

If Jesus intended to reference the supernatural "sons of God" element, the Lot parallel would undermine His point, since Sodom's sin (whatever it was) had nothing to do with angel-human offspring.

The only common elements are: 1. Ordinary life activities (eating, drinking, marrying, business) 2. Spiritual unawareness/unconcern 3. Sudden, complete destruction 4. A righteous person preserved (Noah, Lot)

docs.title: Genesis 6 Elements Jesus Could Have Referenced
docs.text:
If Jesus wanted to emphasize the supernatural aspect of Noah's days, He had clear options:

Genesis 6 Element Available for Reference Jesus Used? "Sons of God" Yes (6:2, 4) NO "Daughters of men" Yes (6:2, 4) NO "Giants/Nephilim" Yes (6:4) NO "Mighty men" Yes (6:4) NO "Men of renown" Yes (6:4) NO Wickedness of man Yes (6:5) NO Evil imagination Yes (6:5) NO Grieved God Yes (6:6) NO Corruption Yes (6:11-12) NO Violence Yes (6:11, 13) NO

Instead, Jesus emphasized elements NOT prominent in Genesis 6: - Eating and drinking (not mentioned in Genesis 6) - Ordinary marrying (Genesis 6:2 has different context) - Unawareness/ignorance (not emphasized in Genesis 6)

docs.title: Why the Silence Matters
docs.text: Jesus was speaking to a Jewish audience familiar with Genesis. If the "sons of God" narrative was His point, He would have mentioned it. His silence on this element - combined with His explicit explanation of what He DID mean - is interpretively decisive.

docs.title: Context: Olivet Discourse (Matthew 24)
docs.text:
Jesus is answering: "What shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?" (Matthew 24:3)

His "days of Noah" teaching serves to warn about: 1. Unknowability of timing - "of that day and hour knoweth no man" (v.36) 2. Normalcy before judgment - life continues as usual (v.38) 3. Sudden interruption - "knew not until the flood came" (v.39) 4. Need for watchfulness - "Watch therefore" (v.42) 5. Need for readiness - "be ye also ready" (v.44)

docs.title: What Would the Supernatural View Contribute?
docs.text:
If Jesus meant to reference angel-human mixing, what would be the application?

If Supernatural View Implied Application Angels mixed with humans Watch for... angels mixing with humans? Nephilim existed Watch for... giants? Bloodlines corrupted Watch for... genetic corruption?

None of these fit Jesus's actual application: "Watch therefore" and "be ye also ready."

docs.title: What the Ordinary Life View Contributes
docs.text:
If Ordinary Life View Implied Application People were living normal lives Don't be caught up in ordinary life People were unaware Stay spiritually aware Judgment came suddenly Be ready at all times Only Noah was prepared Be like Noah - prepared

This perfectly matches Jesus's actual application.

docs.title: The "Marrying and Giving in Marriage" Question
Does This Reference Genesis 6:2?
docs.text:
Some argue that "marrying and giving in marriage" alludes to Genesis 6:2 where the "sons of God" took wives.

Analysis:

Genesis 6:2 Marriage Matthew 24:38 Marriage "Sons of God" taking daughters of men General population marrying Unusual/problematic union Normal social activity Described negatively (contextually) Listed alongside eating/drinking Unique to Noah's time Parallel with Lot's time (no such element)

Key evidence: The Lot parallel destroys this connection.

Luke 17:28 describes Lot's days: "they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded."

Notice: Luke substitutes "buying and selling" for "marrying" when describing Lot's days. This shows: 1. Jesus was listing categories of ordinary activity, not alluding to specific Genesis events 2. The activities are interchangeable examples of normal life 3. No special significance attaches to "marrying" in Jesus's teaching

docs.title: From genesis-6-sons-of-god Study
docs.text:
That study concluded the Sethite view (sons of God = godly line of Seth) is better supported than the angel view: - Genesis 6:3 calls them "flesh" - human terminology - Jesus taught angels don't marry (Matt 22:30) - Moses never uses "bene elohim" for angels elsewhere

Relevance: Even if Genesis 6 refers to human intermarriage (Sethite view), Jesus did not reference this. His point was not about the TYPE of marrying but about ORDINARY marrying continuing until sudden judgment.

docs.title: From hebrew-greek-sons-of-god-comparison Study
docs.text:
That study established: - "Sons of God" language applies to humans in both testaments - The phrase is linguistically compatible with human reference

Relevance: Regardless of how one interprets Genesis 6, Jesus's "days of Noah" teaching does not depend on any particular interpretation of "sons of God."

docs.title: Evidence for Ordinary Life View
docs.text:
1. Jesus's own explanation - He defined "days of Noah" as eating, drinking, marrying, ignorance
  2. The Lot parallel - Proves the point is ordinary life + sudden judgment (no supernatural element)
  3. Jesus's application - "Watch" and "be ready" fits ordinary life view
  4. Silence on supernatural - Jesus mentioned none of the Genesis 6 supernatural elements
  5. Audience relevance - Ordinary life view applies to all generations

docs.title: Evidence Against Supernatural View
docs.text:
1. Jesus never mentioned it - No sons of God, Nephilim, or angels referenced
  2. Lot parallel contradicts it - Sodom had no such element, yet Jesus says "likewise"
  3. Application doesn't fit - "Watch for angel-human mixing" makes no sense
  4. Elements Jesus emphasized - All are ordinary, non-supernatural activities
  5. Explanatory conjunction - γάρ shows Jesus is defining what He means

docs.title: Conclusion of Analysis
docs.text:
Jesus was NOT referring to angels mixing with humans. He was warning that:

  1. Before His coming, life will seem normal
  2. People will be absorbed in ordinary activities
  3. They will be spiritually unaware
  4. Judgment will come suddenly and completely
  5. Only those who are "watching" and "ready" will be preserved

The "days of Noah" reference serves to illustrate sudden judgment interrupting ordinary life, not to reference any supernatural event.

docs.title: Key Greek Terms in Jesus's Teaching
γάρ (gar) - G1063
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:38 - "For as in the days that were before the flood..."

Definition: A primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification)

Significance: - This conjunction introduces Jesus's explanation of what "days of Noah" means - It signals: "What I mean by 'days of Noah' is this..." - The activities Jesus lists (eating, drinking, marrying) are His authoritative definition

Translation: "for," "because," "indeed"

docs.title: ἐσθίω (esthio) - G2068
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:38 - "they were eating" (τρώγοντες) Location: Luke 17:27 - "They did eat" (ἤσθιον)

Definition: To eat (usually literal)

Usage in Context: - Basic human activity of consuming food - Not a metaphor or symbol - Represents ordinary daily life

Significance: Jesus chose the most basic human activity to characterize Noah's days - sustenance. This is universal and timeless.

docs.title: πίνω (pino) - G4095
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:38 - "drinking" (πίνοντες) Location: Luke 17:27 - "they drank" (ἔπινον)

Definition: To imbibe (literally or figuratively)

Usage in Context: - Basic human activity paired with eating - Not specifically referring to drunkenness - Simply normal consumption

Significance: Like eating, drinking is universal and ordinary. Jesus did not emphasize excess or sin but normalcy.

docs.title: γαμέω (gameo) - G1060
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:38 - "marrying" (γαμοῦντες) Location: Luke 17:27 - "they married wives" (ἐγάμουν)

Definition: To wed (of either sex)

Usage Pattern in NT: - Matthew 19:10 - disciples ask about marrying - Matthew 22:30 - angels don't marry (ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν) - 1 Corinthians 7:28 - "if thou marry, thou hast not sinned"

Significance: - Standard word for marriage throughout NT - In Matthew 24:38, paired with eating/drinking as normal activity - NOT a technical term for Genesis 6 "took wives" - Jesus's point: ordinary social arrangements continue until judgment

docs.title: ἐκγαμίζω (ekgamizo) - G1547
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:38 - "giving in marriage" (ἐκγαμίζοντες) Location: Luke 17:27 - "they were given in marriage" (ἐξεγαμίζοντο)

Definition: To marry off a daughter

Usage Pattern: - Matthew 22:30 - "nor are given in marriage" (οὔτε ἐκγαμίζονται) - 1 Corinthians 7:38 - "he that giveth her in marriage doeth well"

Significance: - Refers to the family arrangement of giving daughters in marriage - Represents normal social/family activity - Paired with γαμέω to cover both sides of wedding arrangements

docs.title: οἶδα (oida) - G1492
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:39 - "And knew not" (οὐκ ἔγνωσαν)

Note: Matthew uses γινώσκω (ginosko, G1097) here, a synonym.

Definition: To know, perceive, understand

Usage in Context: - "Knew not until the flood came" - Emphasizes unawareness or lack of perception - Not intellectual ignorance but spiritual unconcern

Significance: This is central to Jesus's point. The people were: - Not watching for judgment - Not spiritually alert - Living as if judgment would never come - Caught completely unaware

docs.title: ὁμοίως (homoios) - G3668
docs.text:
Location: Luke 17:28 - "Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot"

Definition: In like manner, similarly, likewise

Significance: - Jesus draws a direct parallel between Noah and Lot - Whatever characterized Noah's days FOR THIS TEACHING also characterized Lot's days - Since Lot's days had no "sons of God" element, neither does Jesus's point about Noah's days

This word is interpretively crucial - it proves Jesus's point is about common elements (ordinary life, sudden judgment), not unique elements (supernatural activity).

docs.title: γρηγορέω (gregoreo) - G1127
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:42 - "Watch therefore"

Definition: To keep awake, be vigilant, watchful

Usage Pattern: - Matthew 26:38 - "tarry ye here, and watch with me" - Mark 13:35 - "Watch ye therefore" - 1 Thessalonians 5:6 - "let us watch and be sober"

Significance: This is Jesus's application. The response to "days of Noah" is: - Stay spiritually awake - Be vigilant - Don't be caught unaware like those in Noah's day

This application makes sense ONLY if Jesus's point was about unawareness. If His point was about supernatural activity, "watch" would be an odd response.

docs.title: ἕτοιμος (hetoimos) - G2092
docs.text:
Location: Matthew 24:44 - "be ye also ready"

Definition: Adjusted, prepared, ready

Usage Pattern: - Matthew 25:10 - "they that were ready went in" - Luke 12:40 - "be ye therefore ready also" - 1 Peter 3:15 - "be ready always to give an answer"

Significance: Second application from Jesus. Be: - Prepared - In a state of readiness - Not caught off-guard

Again, this application makes sense only if the danger is unexpected timing, not supernatural phenomena.

docs.title: Word Study Summary
docs.text: Greek Word English What It Shows γάρ (gar) "for" Jesus is explaining what "days of Noah" means ἐσθίω (esthio) "eating" Ordinary, universal activity πίνω (pino) "drinking" Ordinary, universal activity γαμέω (gameo) "marrying" Normal word for marriage, not technical ἐκγαμίζω (ekgamizo) "giving in marriage" Normal family arrangements γινώσκω (ginosko) "knew" Unawareness is the problem ὁμοίως (homoios) "likewise" Noah and Lot parallel - same point γρηγορέω (gregoreo) "watch" Application: stay alert ἕτοιμος (hetoimos) "ready" Application: be prepared

docs.title: Conclusion from Word Studies
docs.text:
The Greek vocabulary confirms Jesus's point was about: 1. Ordinary activities (eating, drinking, marrying) - not supernatural events 2. Spiritual unawareness (knew not) - the problem being addressed 3. Parallel with Lot (likewise) - proving the point is common, not unique to Noah 4. Watchfulness and readiness (watch, ready) - the practical response

None of the vocabulary suggests Jesus was referencing Genesis 6's "sons of God" or any supernatural element.

docs.title: What Did Jesus Mean by "As the Days of Noah"?
Question
docs.text: What did Jesus mean by "as the days of Noah" in Matthew 24:37? Was He referring to angels mixing with humans (Genesis 6 "sons of God"), or something else entirely?

docs.title: Summary Answer
docs.text:
Jesus was NOT referring to angels mixing with humans. He was warning that life will seem ordinary before His return, people will be spiritually unaware, and judgment will come suddenly and unexpectedly.

Jesus Himself defined what He meant by "days of Noah": eating, drinking, marrying, giving in marriage, and knowing not until the flood came. He made no mention of sons of God, daughters of men, Nephilim, angels, or any supernatural element.

docs.title: Jesus's Explanation (Matthew 24:37-39)
docs.text: "But as the days of Noe [were], so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be."

docs.title: The Lot Parallel (Luke 17:26-30)
docs.text: "And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man. They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage... Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded; But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom... destroyed [them] all. Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed."

docs.title: What Jesus Emphasized
docs.text: Jesus's Description Category Eating Ordinary activity Drinking Ordinary activity Marrying Ordinary activity Giving in marriage Ordinary activity "Knew not" Spiritual unawareness Flood came suddenly Unexpected judgment Took them all away Complete destruction

docs.title: What Jesus Did NOT Mention
docs.text: Genesis 6 Element In Jesus's Teaching? "Sons of God" NO "Daughters of men" NO Nephilim/Giants NO Angels NO Supernatural mixing NO Unusual wickedness NO Corruption of flesh NO

docs.title: The Decisive Evidence: Lot Parallel
docs.text:
Jesus explicitly paralleled Noah's days with Lot's days: - "Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot" - "Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed"

Lot's days had: - Eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building - Sudden destruction - A righteous person preserved

Lot's days did NOT have: - Sons of God - Nephilim - Angel-human mixing

If Jesus intended to reference the supernatural element, the Lot parallel would contradict His point. The common elements between Noah and Lot are: 1. Ordinary life activities 2. Spiritual unawareness 3. Sudden, complete judgment 4. A righteous person preserved

docs.title: Jesus's Application
docs.text:
"Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come." (Matthew 24:42)

"Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh." (Matthew 24:44)

The application makes sense ONLY if Jesus's point was about unawareness and ordinary life continuing until sudden judgment. If His point was about supernatural activity, "watch" and "be ready" would be strange responses.

docs.title: From genesis-6-sons-of-god Study
docs.text:
That study found the Sethite view (sons of God = godly line of Seth) better supported than the angel view. Key finding: Genesis 6:3 calls the sons of God "flesh" - human terminology.

Relevance to this study: Regardless of how one interprets Genesis 6, Jesus's teaching does not depend on any particular interpretation. He simply did not reference that element.

docs.title: From hebrew-greek-sons-of-god-comparison Study
docs.text:
That study established that "sons of God" language applies to humans in both testaments.

Relevance to this study: Even accepting that Genesis 6 refers to humans (Sethite view), Jesus still did not reference this. His point was about ORDINARY marrying, not any specific type of problematic marriage.

docs.title: What "Days of Noah" Means in Jesus's Teaching
docs.text: Element Meaning "Days of Noah" A time of ordinary life before sudden judgment "Eating and drinking" Life continues as usual "Marrying and giving in marriage" Social arrangements proceed normally "Knew not" Spiritual unawareness/unconcern "Until the flood came" Judgment arrives unexpectedly "Took them all away" Complete destruction of the unprepared

docs.title: What "Days of Noah" Does NOT Mean
docs.text: Jesus was NOT teaching about: - Angel-human hybridization - Nephilim or giants - Genetic corruption - Supernatural wickedness - Any element unique to Noah's time (since Lot's days are parallel)

docs.title: The Bottom Line
docs.text:
Jesus chose what elements of Noah's days to emphasize. He selected: - Ordinary activities (eating, drinking, marrying) - Spiritual unawareness ("knew not") - Sudden judgment

He omitted: - Everything related to Genesis 6:1-4's "sons of God"

This was a deliberate interpretive choice by Jesus. His point was universal and timeless: before judgment comes, people will be living ordinary lives, spiritually unaware, just as in Noah's day and Lot's day. Therefore, watch and be ready.

docs.title: Topics Research: Moses's Terminology for Angels
Question
docs.text: How does Moses refer to angels (celestial beings) in the Pentateuch (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy)?

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: To document what terminology Moses actually uses when referring to celestial beings - without making assumptions or comparisons.

docs.title: ANGEL Topic - Key Pentateuch References
docs.text:
"Angel of the LORD" / "Angel of God": - GEN 16:7,9; 22:11; EXO 3:2; NUM 22:23,25,27,32,35

"Angels of God" (plural): - GEN 28:12; 32:1

"Hosts" (celestial): - GEN 2:1; 32:2

docs.title: CHERUBIM Topic - Pentateuch References
docs.text:
• GEN 3:24 - guarding Eden
  • EXO 25:18-20; 37:7-9 - on the ark
  • EXO 26:1,31; 36:8,35 - on tabernacle curtains

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
1. Search all occurrences of "angel/angels" in the Pentateuch
  2. Search all occurrences of "cherub/cherubim"
  3. Search all occurrences of "host" (celestial context)
  4. Document ONLY what Moses wrote - no interpretation

docs.title: Category 7: What Moses Does NOT Use
Terms NOT used by Moses for celestial beings in the Pentateuch:
docs.text:
• "Sons of God" (bene elohim) - NOT used for angels
  • "Morning stars" - NOT used (appears in Job 38:7)
  • "Holy ones" - NOT used for angels
  • "Watchers" - NOT used (appears in Daniel)
  • "Spirits" - NOT used for angels

docs.title: Summary: Moses's Vocabulary for Celestial Beings
docs.text:
Term Hebrew Occurrences Angel of the LORD malak YHWH 14 times Angel of God malak elohim 3 times Angels (plural) malakim 4 times His/mine/an angel malak 7 times Cherubim/cherub keruvim/keruv 18 times Host (celestial) tsaba 4 times

Total: Moses consistently uses "angel" (malak) or "cherubim" (keruv) when referring to celestial beings.

docs.title: Summary of Findings
docs.text: Moses, in the Pentateuch, uses the following terms for celestial beings:

docs.title: Primary Terms
docs.text: Term Hebrew Usage Angel of the LORD malak YHWH The most common term (14 occurrences) Angel of God malak elohim 3 occurrences Angels (plural) malakim When multiple celestial beings appear (4 occurrences) An angel / his angel / mine angel malak Generic references (7 occurrences) Cherubim / Cherub keruvim / keruv Specific class of celestial beings (18 occurrences) Host (celestial) tsaba Collective term for heavenly beings (4 occurrences)

docs.title: Contexts of Usage
docs.text:
"Angel of the LORD" appears when: - Speaking to Hagar (Gen 16) - Stopping Abraham from sacrificing Isaac (Gen 22) - Appearing to Moses at the burning bush (Exo 3) - Confronting Balaam (Num 22)

"Angels" (plural) appears when: - Two angels visit Sodom (Gen 19) - Jacob sees angels ascending/descending on ladder (Gen 28) - Angels meet Jacob at Mahanaim (Gen 32)

"Cherubim" appears when: - Guarding the garden of Eden (Gen 3) - On the mercy seat and tabernacle furnishings (Exo 25, 26, 36, 37)

"Host of heaven" appears when: - Referring to created celestial bodies/beings (Gen 2:1) - Warning against worship of celestial objects (Deu 4:19; 17:3)

docs.title: Key Observation
docs.text:
Moses consistently uses "angel" (malak) when referring to celestial messengers.

Throughout the Pentateuch, whenever Moses describes a celestial being interacting with humans, he uses: - malak YHWH (angel of the LORD) - malak elohim (angel of God) - malakim (angels)

He does NOT use: - "Sons of God" (bene elohim) - "Spirits" - "Holy ones" - "Watchers" - Other terminology

docs.title: Leviticus - No Angel References
docs.text: Notably, Leviticus contains no references to angels. This book focuses on laws, sacrifices, and priestly duties rather than narrative accounts of angelic appearances.

docs.title: What This Study Documents
docs.text:
This study simply documents Moses's vocabulary. It shows:

  1. Moses had a clear, consistent term for celestial beings: malak (angel/messenger)
  2. Moses used cherubim for a specific class of celestial beings
  3. Moses used host (tsaba) as a collective term
  4. Moses did NOT use "sons of God" for angels anywhere in the Pentateuch

docs.title: No Interpretive Claims
docs.text:
This study makes no claims about: - What "sons of God" in Genesis 6:2 means - Whether angels can or cannot take human form - The relationship between different angelic terms

It simply documents what terminology Moses actually used when he wanted to refer to celestial beings.

docs.title: What This Study Documents
docs.text:
This study documents Moses's vocabulary. It shows:

  1. Moses uses "my people" most frequently for Israel's collective relationship with God
  2. Moses uses "my servant" for individuals (Abraham, Moses, Caleb)
  3. Moses uses "children of the LORD your God" once for Israel (Deu 14:1)
  4. Moses uses "sons of God" twice, both in Genesis 6:2,4
  5. Moses uses "holy people/nation" for Israel's covenant status
  6. Moses uses "chosen" and "peculiar treasure/people" for Israel's election

docs.title: Terms Moses uses for Israel as God's children:
docs.text:
• "Children of the LORD your God" (Deu 14:1) - uses "bene" (children/sons)
  • "My servants" (Lev 25:42,55)
  • "My people" (many times)

docs.title: Terms Moses uses for godly individuals:
docs.text:
• "My servant" - Abraham, Moses, Caleb
  • "Servant of the LORD" - Moses
  • "Man of God" - Moses
  • "Prophet/prophetess" - Abraham, Aaron, Miriam

docs.title: "Sons of God" occurrences:
docs.text:
• Only in Genesis 6:2 and 6:4
  • Context: before the flood
  • No other Pentateuch usage

docs.title: No Interpretive Claims
docs.text:
This study makes no claims about: - What "sons of God" in Genesis 6:2,4 refers to - Whether the term refers to angels, humans, or another category - The relationship between "sons of God" and other terminology

It simply documents what terminology Moses actually used when referring to humans in relationship with God.

docs.title: Verse Analysis: Origin of the Nephilim
Genesis 6:4
docs.text:
Context: Immediately before the flood narrative. The "sons of God" have taken wives from the "daughters of men."

Direct statement:

"There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare [children] to them, the same [became] mighty men which [were] of old, men of renown."

Key observations:

  1. Timing phrase "in those days; and also after that":
  2. "In those days" = Nephilim existed BEFORE the unions began
  3. "And also after that" = Nephilim continued to exist AFTER the unions

  4. Critical: If Nephilim were the OFFSPRING of these unions, they could only exist AFTER, not BEFORE

  5. "When the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men":

  6. This describes WHEN the Nephilim existed, not HOW they originated

  7. The text does NOT say "and the sons of God produced Nephilim"

  8. "The same became mighty men":

  9. "The same" refers to "children" born from the unions
  10. These children became "mighty men... men of renown"

  11. NOT the same as "giants" (nephilim) mentioned earlier in the verse

  12. Structure of the verse:

  13. Statement: Nephilim existed in those days and after
  14. Context: When sons of God took daughters of men
  15. Result: Children born to them became mighty men of renown
  16. The Nephilim and the "mighty men of renown" appear to be distinct groups

Conclusion: Genesis 6:4 does NOT state that Nephilim were offspring of the "sons of God." It states they existed in that era and continued afterward. The timing language is fatal to the hybrid theory.

docs.title: Numbers 13:33
docs.text:
Context: Twelve spies return from Canaan. Ten give a fearful report.

Direct statement:

"And there we saw the giants [nephilim], the sons of Anak, [which come] of the giants [nephilim]..."

Key observations:

  1. Post-flood Nephilim:
  2. The spies use "nephilim" for people they saw in Canaan

  3. This is after the flood that supposedly destroyed all Nephilim

  4. Human lineage stated:

  5. "Sons of Anak" - traced to a human father
  6. "Which come of the giants" - they descended from earlier large people

  7. No angel connection mentioned

  8. Known genealogy:

  9. Numbers 13:22: "Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak"
  10. Joshua 15:13: "Arba the father of Anak"
  11. Lineage: Arba > Anak > Sheshai, Ahiman, Talmai

Critical question: If "nephilim" requires angel parentage, how did they exist after the flood? The angel view must either: - Claim angels produced offspring again after the flood (no biblical evidence) - Claim some nephilim survived the flood (contradicts purpose of flood) - Admit "nephilim" simply means "giants" without requiring angel parentage

Conclusion: The use of "nephilim" for the Anakim - whose human genealogy is known - proves the term means "giants," not "angel-human hybrids."

docs.title: Pattern Analysis
docs.text:
Person Lifespan Multiple of Modern (~80 years) Adam 930 years 11.6x Seth 912 years 11.4x Enos 905 years 11.3x Cainan 910 years 11.4x Mahalaleel 895 years 11.2x Jared 962 years 12.0x Methuselah 969 years 12.1x Lamech 777 years 9.7x Noah 950 years 11.9x

Key observations:

  1. Consistent pattern: Pre-flood humans lived 10-12 times longer than modern humans
  2. Gradual decline after flood: Post-flood lifespans decreased over generations
  3. Biological implication: Longer lifespan = more growth time = larger potential size

Scientific parallel: - Longer-lived organisms often achieve greater size - Reptiles and fish continue growing throughout life - Pre-flood conditions may have allowed extended human growth

Conclusion: The extraordinary lifespans of pre-flood humans provide a natural explanation for larger body sizes without requiring supernatural hybridization.

docs.title: The Zamzummims (Deuteronomy 2:20-21)
docs.text:
Context: Moses describing the Ammonite territory.

Direct statement:

"That also was accounted a land of giants: giants dwelt therein in old time; and the Ammonites call them Zamzummims; A people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the LORD destroyed them before them..."

Key observations: - Called "a people" - human tribe - Same description: "great, and many, and tall" - Destroyed by "the LORD" - mortal beings who could be killed - Given tribal name by Ammonites - No angel connection mentioned

docs.title: The Anakim (Multiple passages)
docs.text:
Traced genealogy: - Joshua 14:15: "Arba was a great man among the Anakims" - Joshua 15:13: "Arba the father of Anak" - Joshua 15:14: "Three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai"

Family tree: 

Arba ("a great man")
  └── Anak
       ├── Sheshai
       ├── Ahiman
       └── Talmai

Key observations: - Arba explicitly called "a great man" - human - Complete human genealogy provided - Defeated by Joshua and Caleb - mortal - Remnant in Gaza, Gath, Ashdod (Josh 11:22) - No angel connection mentioned

docs.title: Og King of Bashan (Deuteronomy 3:11)
docs.text:
Direct statement:

"For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron... nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man."

Key observations: - "Remnant of giants" - descended from earlier large people - Bed: ~13.5 feet long, ~6 feet wide (suggests great size) - "Cubit of a man" - human measurement - Human king of a human kingdom - Defeated by Moses - mortal - No angel connection mentioned

docs.title: Goliath (1 Samuel 17:4)
docs.text:
Direct statement:

"There went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span."

Key observations: - Height: ~9.5 feet (some manuscripts say 4 cubits = ~6.5 feet) - "Philistine" - human ethnicity - "Of Gath" - from a city (same area Anakim remained, Josh 11:22) - Killed by David with a stone - mortal - No angel connection mentioned

docs.title: Giants of Gath (2 Samuel 21:16-22)
docs.text:
Direct statement:

"These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants."

Key observations: - Four giants: Ishbibenob, Saph, unnamed (with polydactyly), and Goliath's brother - All "sons of the giant" - human family lineage - One had six fingers/toes - genetic condition (polydactyly) - All killed in battle - mortal humans - From Gath - consistent with Anakim remnant location - No angel connection mentioned

docs.title: Pattern 1: Human Terminology
docs.text: Every post-flood giant is described using human terms: - "A people" (Emims, Zamzummims) - "A man" (Arba, Og) - "Sons of" with human father (sons of Anak, sons of the giant) - Human ethnic identities (Philistine, Moabite names, etc.)

docs.title: Pattern 2: Traceable Genealogies
docs.text: Where lineage is given, it is always human: - Anakim: Arba > Anak > three sons - Giants of Gath: "Born to the giant" - human family

docs.title: Pattern 3: Mortality
docs.text: All giants died by normal means: - Destroyed by the LORD (Zamzummims) - Defeated by Joshua, Caleb, Moses, David - Killed with weapons (stone, sword)

docs.title: Pattern 4: No Angel References
docs.text: In all passages describing giants: - No mention of angel parentage - No supernatural origin claimed - No special means required to defeat them

docs.title: Pattern 5: Geographic Continuity
docs.text: Giants found where Anakim remained: - Joshua 11:22: Anakim remnant in Gaza, Gath, Ashdod - 1 Samuel 17:4: Goliath from Gath - 2 Samuel 21: Giants of Gath

docs.title: Connections Between Passages
docs.text:
1. Genesis 6:4 → Numbers 13:33: Both use "nephilim," but Numbers identifies them as Anakim with human genealogy

  2. Numbers 13:22 → Joshua 15:13-14: Same three sons of Anak named; human lineage confirmed

  3. Joshua 11:22 → 1 Samuel 17; 2 Samuel 21: Anakim remnant in Gath connects to later giants from Gath

  4. Deuteronomy 2 parallels: Emims, Zamzummims, and Anakim all described identically - tall human peoples

  5. Genesis 5 → Genesis 6: Pre-flood lifespans provide context for larger pre-flood humans

docs.title: Findings Summary
docs.text: Finding Evidence Nephilim existed BEFORE "sons of God" unions Genesis 6:4 timing "Nephilim" used for humans with known genealogy Numbers 13:33; Josh 15:13-14 All post-flood giants have human lineages Multiple passages No giant is attributed to angel parentage All passages silent Pre-flood conditions favored larger size Genesis 5 lifespans Giants were mortal All defeated in battle

docs.title: Word Studies: Origin of the Nephilim
Strong's H5303
docs.text:
Hebrew: נָפִיל (naphil), plural: נְפִלִים (nephilim)

Transliteration: naphil / nephilim

Pronunciation: nef-eel'

Part of Speech: Masculine noun

Root/Etymology: From נָפַל (naphal, H5307) = "to fall"

Definition: According to Strong's: "a feller, i.e. a bully or tyrant" - translated as "giant"

docs.title: All Biblical Occurrences
docs.text:
Reference Hebrew KJV Translation Context Genesis 6:4 הַנְּפִלִים giants Pre-flood era Numbers 13:33 (2x) הַנְּפִילִם giants Spies' report of Canaan

Total occurrences: 3 (in 2 verses)

docs.title: Interpretation Options
docs.text:
1. "Fallen ones" - from root naphal (to fall)
  2. Could mean: those who fell morally
  3. Or: those who cause others to fall (tyrants)

  4. Or: the offspring of those who fell (angel view interpretation)

  5. "Giants" - physical stature

  6. Septuagint (LXX) translates as γίγαντες (gigantes)
  7. Numbers 13:33 clearly associates with large stature

  8. Context in both passages involves size/power

  9. "Mighty men / Tyrants" - Strong's primary definition

  10. "A feller, i.e. a bully or tyrant"
  11. Genesis 6:4 describes them as "mighty men... men of renown"

docs.title: Critical Observation
docs.text:
The root naphal means "to fall" - but the angel view assumes this refers to "fallen angels." However:

  1. The word is used of the Anakim in Numbers 13:33
  2. The Anakim have a known human genealogy (Arba > Anak > sons)
  3. If "nephilim" required angel parentage, it couldn't apply to the Anakim

Conclusion: "Nephilim" describes a TYPE of person (giants/tyrants), not an ORIGIN (angel-human hybrids).

docs.title: Strong's H7497
docs.text:
Hebrew: רְפָאִים (rephaim)

Transliteration: repha'im

Pronunciation: raw-faw'

Definition: "Giants, Rephaim" - an old tribe of giants, ancient inhabitants of Canaan

Root: From H7495 רָפָא (rapha) = "to heal, to invigorate"

docs.title: KJV Usage
docs.text: Translation Occurrences "giant(s)" 17 times "Rephaim" 8 times Total 25 times

docs.title: Key Occurrences
docs.text: Reference Context Genesis 14:5 Rephaims smitten by Chedorlaomer Genesis 15:20 Listed among Canaanite peoples Deuteronomy 2:11 Compared to Anakim Deuteronomy 2:20 Zamzummims "accounted" Rephaim Deuteronomy 3:11 Og, last of the Rephaim Joshua 12:4; 13:12 Og's territory Joshua 17:15 Land of the Rephaim

docs.text:

  3. Human king: Og is called "remnant of the Rephaim" but rules a human kingdom
  4. No angel connection: Never attributed to angel parentage

Joshua 15:13: "Arba the father of Anak"

Joshua 15:14: "The three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak"

docs.text:
1. Arba explicitly called "a man" - not angel, not hybrid
  2. Complete human genealogy - father to sons traceable
  3. Called "nephilim" in Numbers 13:33 - proves nephilim = giants, not hybrids

docs.text:
Hebrew: רָפָה (Raphah)

Transliteration: raphah

Pronunciation: raw-faw'

Definition: A Philistine giant, ancestor of several giants in David's time

docs.title: 2 Samuel 21 Usage
docs.text: v. 16: "Ishbibenob, which [was] of the sons of the giant [H7497]" v. 18: "Saph, which [was] of the sons of the giant [H7497]" v. 20: "he also was born to the giant [H7498]" v. 22: "These four were born to the giant [H7498] in Gath"

docs.title: Significance
docs.text:
1. "Born to" - human birth language
  2. "Sons of the giant" - family lineage, not supernatural origin
  3. "The giant" (H7498) - a specific person, their ancestor
  4. From Gath - same location where Anakim remnant remained (Josh 11:22)

Conclusion: The giants of Gath were descendants of a human giant ancestor, not angel-human hybrids. The language is consistently human family terminology.

This phrase confirms: 1. Human measurement standards apply 2. Og was large but measured by human standards 3. No supernatural scale required
