docs.title: The Term "Nephilim" in Numbers 13:33
docs.text:
The spies called the Anakim "nephilim." But we know: - The Anakim descended from Arba (human) - Arba fathered Anak (human genealogy) - Anak fathered Sheshai, Ahiman, Talmai (human family)

If "nephilim" required angel parentage: - The term could NOT apply to the Anakim - But the inspired text DOES apply it to them

Therefore: "Nephilim" describes physical/social characteristics (giants, tyrants), NOT origin (angel-human hybrids).

docs.title: Connection to genesis-6-sons-of-god Word Studies
docs.text:
The prerequisite study (04-word-studies.md) already established:

  1. "bene elohim" is rare - only 5 OT occurrences
  2. Context differs - Job describes heavenly scenes; Genesis describes human affairs
  3. God calls them "flesh" (Gen 6:3) - unusual for angels
  4. Nephilim existed "before" and "after" - problematic for hybrid view

This study confirms: The word "nephilim" itself does not require angel parentage, as proven by its application to the Anakim.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: The angel view claims the Nephilim were angel-human hybrids, explaining their extraordinary size. If the "sons of God" were just humans (Sethite view), how do we explain the giants?

docs.title: Summary Answer
docs.text: The biblical evidence shows that Nephilim were not angel-human hybrids. Genesis 6:4 explicitly states Nephilim existed BEFORE the "sons of God" unions began, which is fatal to the hybrid theory. Furthermore, post-flood "nephilim" (the Anakim) have fully traceable human genealogies, and the extraordinary pre-flood lifespans (800-970 years) provide a natural explanation for larger body sizes.

docs.title: Key Verses
docs.text:
Genesis 6:4 - "There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare [children] to them, the same [became] mighty men which [were] of old, men of renown."

Numbers 13:33 - "And there we saw the giants [nephilim], the sons of Anak, which come of the giants [nephilim]..."

Joshua 15:13-14 - "...the city of Arba the father of Anak... And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak."

Genesis 5:27 - "And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died."

docs.title: 1. The Timing Problem (Genesis 6:4)
docs.text:
The most decisive evidence against the hybrid theory is the timing phrase in Genesis 6:4:

"There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that..."

This means Nephilim existed: - BEFORE the "sons of God" took wives ("in those days") - AFTER the unions ("and also after that")

If Nephilim were the offspring of these unions, they could only exist AFTER, not before. The text explicitly states they pre-existed the unions. This is fatal to the hybrid theory.

docs.title: 2. Post-Flood "Nephilim" Have Human Genealogies
docs.text:
The spies in Numbers 13:33 called the Anakim "nephilim." But we know the Anakim's lineage:

Arba ("a great man among the Anakims" - Josh 14:15)
  └── Anak
       ├── Sheshai
       ├── Ahiman
       └── Talmai

If "nephilim" required angel parentage, the term could not apply to the Anakim. But Scripture does apply it. This proves "nephilim" simply means "giants," not "angel-human hybrids."

docs.title: 3. ALL Post-Flood Giants Are Human
docs.text:
Every giant mentioned after the flood has traceable human ancestry:

Giants Lineage Reference Anakim Arba > Anak > 3 sons Josh 15:13-14 Emims "A people great, and many, and tall" Deut 2:10-11 Zamzummims "A people great, and many, and tall" Deut 2:20-21 Og "A man" - king of Bashan Deut 3:11 Goliath Philistine of Gath 1 Sam 17:4 Giants of Gath "Born to the giant" - family 2 Sam 21:16-22

Not one post-flood giant is attributed to angel parentage. All are described using human terms: "a people," "a man," "sons of," "born to."

docs.title: 4. Pre-Flood Lifespans Explain Larger Size
docs.text:
Genesis 5 records pre-flood lifespans of 800-970 years - 10-12 times longer than modern lifespans. Longer life means: - Extended growth periods - More time for physical development - Different environmental conditions

This same pattern appears in the fossil record - ancient creatures were often significantly larger than modern counterparts (larger insects, reptiles, mammals). No supernatural hybridization is required; pre-flood conditions naturally produced larger organisms.

docs.title: 5. The Word "Nephilim" Itself
docs.text:
Strong's H5303 defines nephilim as "a feller, i.e. a bully or tyrant" - translated "giant." The root is naphal ("to fall"), but this doesn't require "fallen angel" origin. It could mean: - Those who fell morally - Those who cause others to fall (tyrants) - Simply a descriptor of their imposing nature

The application of "nephilim" to the Anakim (with known human genealogy) proves the term describes what they WERE (giants/tyrants), not HOW they originated.

docs.title: The Hybrid Theory's Problems
docs.text:
1. Timing contradiction: Nephilim existed BEFORE the "sons of God" unions (Gen 6:4)
  2. Post-flood existence: "Nephilim" in Canaan were Anakim with human genealogy
  3. No angel lineage: Every biblical giant traces to human parents
  4. Natural explanation available: Pre-flood longevity (800-970 years) explains larger size
  5. Fossil parallel: Same size pattern observed in ancient creatures (no angels involved)
  6. Human terminology: All giants called "a people," "a man," "sons of," "born to"

docs.title: Connection to Related Studies
docs.text: Study Key Finding genesis-6-sons-of-god "Sons of God" likely godly Sethite line; Gen 6:3 calls them "flesh" angels-physical-form Angels appearing physically doesn't prove reproductive capability moses-angel-terminology Moses uses "malak" for angels, never "bene elohim"

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The "Nephilim = angel-human hybrids" explanation:

  1. Contradicts Genesis 6:4 timing - Nephilim existed before the unions
  2. Cannot explain post-flood nephilim - Anakim with human genealogies
  3. Ignores natural explanation - Pre-flood longevity produced larger humans
  4. Lacks biblical support - No giant is attributed to angel parentage
  5. Misunderstands the word - "Nephilim" describes what they were, not their origin

The biblical evidence shows Nephilim were simply large, powerful humans - a natural result of pre-flood conditions and genetic variation, not supernatural parentage. The term "nephilim" means "giants" or "tyrants," as proven by its application to the Anakim whose human lineage is explicitly stated.

docs.text: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit. Howbeit that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; and afterward that which is spiritual. The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven. As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly. And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly. Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption. Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?

docs.title: 2 Corinthians 5:1-5
docs.text: For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked. For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life. Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

docs.title: Revelation 21:1-7
docs.text: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful. And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely. He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son.

docs.title: John 1:12-13
docs.text: Context: Prologue to John's Gospel, describing the incarnation of the Word (Christ) and how people responded to him. Direct statement: Those who receive Christ are given "power to become the sons of God" (exousian tekna theou genesthai). They are "born...of God." Key observations: - Uses "power/authority" (exousia) - a right or privilege granted - Uses "become" (genesthai) - indicates a change of state, not inherent status - Sonship is linked to: (1) receiving Christ, (2) believing on his name, (3) being born of God - This is contrasted with natural birth ("not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh") - Timing: Present reality for those who believe

docs.title: Romans 8:14-17
docs.text: Context: Paul discussing life in the Spirit vs. life in the flesh; the contrast between bondage and freedom. Direct statement: "As many as are led by the Spirit of God, they ARE the sons of God" (present tense). They have received "the Spirit of adoption" and ARE "children of God." Key observations: - Present tense: "they ARE" (eisin) - current reality - "Spirit of adoption" (pneuma huiothesias) - adoption is already received - The Spirit is evidence of sonship (crying "Abba, Father") - If children, then heirs - inheritance rights are present - Suffering with Christ leads to being "glorified together" (future) - Timing: Present status, with future glorification

docs.title: Romans 8:19
docs.text: Context: Continuing from v.17-18, Paul discusses present suffering and future glory. Direct statement: Creation "waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God." Key observations: - "Manifestation" (apokalupsin) - an unveiling/revelation of something that exists but is hidden - Believers ARE sons now (v.14), but this is not yet fully manifest - Creation itself awaits this event - Timing: Future event, but presupposes present sonship

docs.title: Romans 8:21
docs.text: Context: Creation's bondage and future deliverance. Direct statement: Creation will be delivered "into the glorious liberty of the children of God." Key observations: - "Glorious liberty" is contrasted with "bondage of corruption" - This liberty belongs to "the children of God" - It's future for creation, suggesting it's also future in its fullness for believers - Timing: Future fullness

docs.title: Romans 8:23
docs.text: Context: Present groaning and future hope. Direct statement: "Waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body." Key observations: - Already have "firstfruits of the Spirit" (present possession) - Yet still "waiting for the adoption" (future aspect) - Adoption is equated with "redemption of our body" (bodily transformation) - This is a key text: adoption has BOTH present and future aspects - Timing: Future aspect of adoption = bodily redemption

docs.title: Philippians 2:15
docs.text: Context: Paul exhorting believers to obedience, unity, and godly living. Direct statement: Believers should be "blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation." Key observations: - Sonship is a PRESENT reality ("sons of God" describes current state) - This is explicitly "in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation" - on earth - They "shine as lights in the world" - earthly context - Timing: Present, explicitly on earth in mortal life

docs.title: 1 John 3:1-2
docs.text: Context: John discussing the love of the Father and the hope of believers. Direct statement: (1) "We should be called the sons of God" (present), (2) "NOW are we the sons of God" (present), (3) "it doth not yet appear what we shall be" (future unknown), (4) "when he shall appear, we shall be like him" (future transformation). Key observations: - Most explicit "now and not yet" passage in NT - Present: we ARE sons of God NOW - Present: the world doesn't recognize us (just as they didn't recognize Christ) - Future: "what we shall be" is not yet apparent - Future: "we shall be like him" when he appears - Timing: Both NOW and NOT YET

docs.title: Matthew 5:9
docs.text: Context: Beatitudes, part of Sermon on the Mount. Direct statement: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they SHALL BE CALLED the children of God." Key observations: - Future tense: "shall be called" (klethesontai) - Peacemaking leads to being called/recognized as God's children - Could refer to future eschatological recognition or ongoing recognition - Timing: Future (either ongoing or eschatological)

docs.title: Matthew 5:45
docs.text: Context: Command to love enemies. Direct statement: "That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven." Key observations: - Purpose clause: loving enemies demonstrates/proves sonship - Imitating the Father's character (rain on just and unjust) marks children - Character conformed to Father = evidence of sonship - Timing: Present character marking present sonship

docs.title: Luke 20:35-36
docs.text: Context: Jesus answering Sadducees about the resurrection; question about marriage. Direct statement: Those who obtain "that world" and "the resurrection from the dead" (1) don't marry, (2) can't die anymore, (3) are "equal unto the angels," (4) are "the children of God, being the children of the resurrection." Key observations: - "Children of God" here is explicitly LINKED to resurrection - "Children of the resurrection" = children of God (parallel phrases) - They become "equal unto the angels" (isangeloi) - angel-like nature - They "cannot die anymore" - immortality - This describes a transformed state AFTER resurrection - Timing: After resurrection, with transformed nature

docs.title: Galatians 3:26
docs.text: Context: Paul arguing that faith, not law, makes one a child of Abraham/God. Direct statement: "For ye ARE all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus." Key observations: - Present tense: "ye ARE" (este) - Basis: "by faith in Christ Jesus" (dia tes pisteos) - Universal among believers: "all" - Timing: Present reality through faith

docs.title: Galatians 4:5-7
docs.text: Context: Contrast between slavery under law and sonship through Christ. Direct statement: Christ came "that we might receive the adoption of sons." Because "ye are sons," God sent the Spirit. "Thou art no more a servant, but a son." Key observations: - Purpose of Christ's redemption: "that we might receive the adoption" - "Ye ARE sons" (present tense) - basis for receiving Spirit - Spirit is evidence of sonship (crying "Abba, Father") - Status change: "no more a servant, but a son" - present change - If son, then heir - inheritance rights - Timing: Present adoption and sonship

docs.title: 1 Corinthians 15:50-53
docs.text: Context: Paul explaining the resurrection body. Direct statement: "Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God." "We shall all be changed." "This mortal must put on immortality." Key observations: - Physical change is REQUIRED for full inheritance - Current body = "flesh and blood," "corruptible," "mortal" - Future body = "incorruptible," "immortal" - "We shall all be changed" - universal transformation needed - Timing: Future, at resurrection

docs.title: Revelation 21:7
docs.text: Context: New heaven and new earth; God dwelling with humanity. Direct statement: "He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son." Key observations: - Ultimate fulfillment of sonship - Linked to overcoming and inheriting - In context of new creation (no more death, tears, pain) - Timing: Future, in new creation

docs.title: Pattern 1: Present Sonship Through Faith
docs.text: Multiple passages affirm believers ARE sons/children of God NOW: - "They ARE the sons of God" (Rom 8:14) - "We ARE the children of God" (Rom 8:16) - "NOW are we the sons of God" (1 John 3:2) - "Ye ARE all the children of God by faith" (Gal 3:26) - "Ye ARE sons" (Gal 4:6) - "Sons of God...in the midst of a crooked nation" (Phil 2:15)

docs.title: Pattern 2: Future Manifestation/Completion
docs.text: Yet something more is awaited: - "Waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God" (Rom 8:19) - "Glorious liberty of the children of God" (Rom 8:21) - "Waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body" (Rom 8:23) - "It doth not yet appear what we shall be" (1 John 3:2) - "We shall be like him" (1 John 3:2) - "Children of the resurrection...cannot die anymore" (Luke 20:36)

docs.title: Pattern 3: Sonship Linked to Spirit
docs.text: The Holy Spirit is consistently connected to present sonship: - "Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15) - "The Spirit beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God" (Rom 8:16) - "God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father" (Gal 4:6)

docs.title: Pattern 4: Physical Transformation Required for Full Inheritance
docs.text:
• "Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom" (1 Cor 15:50)
  • "We shall all be changed" (1 Cor 15:51)
  • "This mortal must put on immortality" (1 Cor 15:53)
  • "Equal unto the angels...cannot die anymore" (Luke 20:36)
  • "We shall be like him" (1 John 3:2)
  • "Redemption of our body" = full adoption (Rom 8:23)

docs.title: Romans 8 Internal Connection
docs.text:
• v.14: "they ARE the sons of God" (present)
  • v.15: "Spirit of adoption" (present experience)
  • v.16: "we ARE children of God" (present)
  • v.19: "manifestation of the sons of God" (future)
  • v.21: "glorious liberty of the children of God" (future)
  • v.23: "waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body" (future)

This single chapter demonstrates BOTH aspects: present sonship AND future completion.

docs.title: 1 John 3:2 as Key Summary
docs.text:
"Beloved, NOW are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him."

This perfectly captures: - Present reality: "NOW are we" - Future mystery: "not yet appear what we shall be" - Future certainty: "we shall be like him"

docs.title: Luke 20:36 + 1 Cor 15:50-53 Connection
docs.text:
Both passages address resurrection transformation: - Luke 20: "equal unto the angels," "cannot die anymore," "children of the resurrection" - 1 Cor 15: "we shall all be changed," "mortal must put on immortality"

The "children of God/resurrection" status in Luke 20 requires the transformation described in 1 Cor 15.

docs.title: Galatians 4 + Romans 8 Connection
docs.text:
Both use "huiothesia" (adoption) and "Abba, Father": - Gal 4:5-6: "receive the adoption of sons...Spirit...crying, Abba, Father" - Rom 8:15: "Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father"

The Spirit's testimony is the present evidence of adoption.

docs.title: huios (G5207) - Son
docs.text: Original: υἱός Transliteration: huios Pronunciation: hwee-os' Definition: A son; used of immediate, remote, or figurative kinship. Apparently a primary word.

docs.title: Meaning and Usage
docs.text: The Greek word huios emphasizes the inward, ethical, and legal aspects of relationship. It denotes: 1. Literal male offspring 2. Descendants/posterity (e.g., "sons of Abraham") 3. Those who belong to or are characterized by something (e.g., "sons of disobedience") 4. Those in a special relationship (e.g., "Son of God" for Christ, believers)

docs.title: Usage in Key Verses
docs.text:
• John 1:12 - "sons of God" (huious theou) - those who receive Christ
  • Romans 8:14 - "sons of God" (huioi theou) - those led by the Spirit
  • Romans 8:19 - "sons of God" (huion tou theou) - awaiting manifestation
  • Philippians 2:15 - "sons of God" (tekna theou in some MSS, but huioi in TR)
  • 1 John 3:1, 2 - "sons of God" (tekna theou) - present reality

docs.title: Significance for This Study
docs.text: When applied to believers, huios emphasizes: - Legal standing (adoption rights) - Ethical character (reflecting the Father) - Inheritance rights (heirs of God)

docs.title: teknon (G5043) - Child
docs.text: Original: τέκνον Transliteration: teknon Pronunciation: tek'-non Definition: A child (as produced); offspring. From the base of G5088 (tikto - to bring forth).

docs.title: Meaning and Usage
docs.text: The Greek word teknon emphasizes the physical and outward aspects of parentage. It denotes: 1. Literal offspring 2. Pupils or disciples (as "children" of their teachers) 3. Those in intimate relationship formed through bonds of love and trust

docs.title: Metaphorical Usage
docs.text:
• "Children of God" (tekna theou) - believers led by God's Spirit
  • "Children of the devil" - those characterized by evil
  • "Children of wisdom" - those nurtured by wisdom
  • "Children of wrath" - those under God's judgment

docs.title: Usage in Key Verses
docs.text:
• John 1:12 - "children of God" (tekna theou) - power to become
  • Romans 8:16, 17, 21 - "children of God" (tekna theou) - Spirit's witness
  • Galatians 3:26 - "children of God" (huioi theou, though KJV translates "children")
  • 1 John 3:1, 2, 10 - "children of God" (tekna theou) - present status

docs.title: Distinction from huios
docs.text:
Aspect huios (son) teknon (child) Emphasis Legal, ethical, inward Physical, relational, outward Focus Status, rights, character Origin, birth, nurture Inheritance Stressed Implied

Both terms are used interchangeably in some contexts (e.g., Romans 8:14 uses huioi, v.16-17 uses tekna), suggesting they overlap significantly when referring to believers.

docs.title: huiothesia (G5206) - Adoption
docs.text: Original: υἱοθεσία Transliteration: huiothesia Pronunciation: hwee-oth-es-ee'-ah Definition: The placing as a son; adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God).

docs.title: Etymology
docs.text:
Compound word: - υἱός (huios) = son - θέσις (thesis, from τίθημι/tithemi) = placing, putting

Literally: "the placing as a son"

docs.title: NT Occurrences (5 total)
docs.text:
1. Romans 8:15 - "Spirit of adoption" (pneuma huiothesias)
  2. Romans 8:23 - "waiting for the adoption" (huiothesian apekdechomenoi)
  3. Romans 9:4 - Israel's adoption (he huiothesia)
  4. Galatians 4:5 - "receive the adoption of sons" (huiothesian apolabomen)
  5. Ephesians 1:5 - "adoption of children" (huiothesian)

docs.title: Three Applications in NT
docs.text:
1. Israel's Covenant Status (Rom 9:4) God's special relationship with Israel as His "son" (cf. Exodus 4:22-23).

2. Present Christian Identity (Rom 8:15; Gal 4:5; Eph 1:5) Believers receive adoption NOW through Christ. Evidence: - Spirit of adoption received - Cry "Abba, Father" - No longer servants but sons

3. Future Fulfillment (Rom 8:23) "Waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body" - Full adoption awaits bodily transformation - Present adoption is "firstfruits" - Complete adoption includes resurrection

docs.title: Significance for This Study
docs.text:
Huiothesia reveals that adoption has TWO PHASES: 1. Present: Received through faith, evidenced by Spirit 2. Future: Completed at resurrection ("redemption of our body")

Romans 8:23 is crucial: believers have "firstfruits of the Spirit" (present) but still await "the adoption, the redemption of our body" (future). The same word (huiothesia) is used for both what they've received (v.15) and what they await (v.23).

docs.title: isangelos (Implied in Luke 20:36)
docs.text: Original: ἰσάγγελος Transliteration: isangelos Pronunciation: ee-sang'-el-os Definition: Like an angel, angel-like.

docs.title: Etymology
docs.text: Compound word: - ἴσος (isos) = equal - ἄγγελος (angelos) = angel, messenger

docs.title: Usage in Luke 20:36
docs.text: "Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels (isangeloi); and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection."

docs.title: Significance for This Study
docs.text:
This describes the FUTURE state of believers after resurrection: - Cannot die anymore (immortal) - Equal to/like angels (transformed nature) - "Children of God" linked to "children of the resurrection"

This confirms that full sonship involves physical transformation to an immortal, angel-like state.

docs.title: Summary: Word Studies and the Question
docs.text:
The Greek terminology confirms the "now and not yet" pattern:

Word Present Aspect Future Aspect huios/teknon Believers ARE sons/children now Full manifestation awaited huiothesia Spirit of adoption received Full adoption = bodily redemption isangelos Not applicable Describes resurrection state

The same word (huiothesia) is used for both present reception and future completion, demonstrating that adoption is a process with distinct phases, not a single event.

docs.title: NT "Sons/Children of God" Applied to Humans
Question
docs.text: Does "sons of God" or "children of God" in the NT refer to humans? If so, when - on earth or after translation to heaven? Does it require a change in their being/humanity/physical form?

docs.title: Summary Answer
docs.text: Yes, the NT clearly and repeatedly applies "sons of God" and "children of God" to human believers. This sonship has two phases: (1) a present spiritual/legal reality received through faith, experienced on earth in mortal bodies, and (2) a future manifestation at resurrection that requires physical transformation from mortality to immortality. The key text is 1 John 3:2: "Beloved, NOW are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him."

docs.title: Present Sonship (On Earth)
docs.text:
"For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they ARE the sons of God." (Romans 8:14)

"The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we ARE the children of God." (Romans 8:16)

"For ye ARE all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus." (Galatians 3:26)

"Beloved, NOW are we the sons of God." (1 John 3:2a)

"That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world." (Philippians 2:15)

docs.title: Future Completion (After Resurrection)
docs.text:
"For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God." (Romans 8:19)

"Waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body." (Romans 8:23)

"It doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him." (1 John 3:2b)

"Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection." (Luke 20:36)

"Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God... We shall all be changed." (1 Corinthians 15:50-51)

docs.title: Question 1: Does "Sons of God" Refer to Humans?
docs.text:
Answer: YES, unambiguously.

The NT uses both "sons of God" (huioi theou) and "children of God" (tekna theou) to describe human believers:

Term Key References Sons of God (huioi theou) John 1:12; Romans 8:14, 19; Philippians 2:15; 1 John 3:1-2 Children of God (tekna theou) Matthew 5:9, 45; Luke 20:36; Romans 8:16, 21; Galatians 3:26; 1 John 3:10

This is distinct from OT usage (Genesis 6, Job 1-2) which may refer to angels. In the NT, the phrase clearly designates human believers.

docs.title: Question 2: When? On Earth or After Translation?
docs.text:
Answer: BOTH - The NT teaches a "now and not yet" sonship.

PRESENT (On Earth, in Mortal Bodies): - Believers ARE sons/children NOW through faith (Gal 3:26) - This is explicitly "in the midst of a crooked nation" (Phil 2:15) - The Spirit testifies to present sonship (Rom 8:16) - The Spirit of adoption is already received (Rom 8:15; Gal 4:5-6)

FUTURE (At Resurrection/Glorification): - Creation awaits "the manifestation of the sons of God" (Rom 8:19) - Full adoption = "the redemption of our body" (Rom 8:23) - "It doth not yet appear what we shall be" (1 John 3:2) - "Children of God, being children of the resurrection" (Luke 20:36)

The Greek word for adoption (huiothesia) appears for both present reception (Rom 8:15) and future completion (Rom 8:23), confirming adoption is a two-phase process.

docs.title: Question 3: Does It Require Physical Change?
docs.text:
Answer: For present sonship, NO. For full manifestation, YES.

Present Sonship - No Physical Change Required: - Received through faith (Gal 3:26) - Through receiving Christ (John 1:12) - Evidenced by the Spirit (Rom 8:16; Gal 4:6) - Exists while in mortal body on earth (Phil 2:15) - Is spiritual, relational, and legal (adoption)

Full Manifestation - Physical Change REQUIRED: The NT explicitly teaches bodily transformation is necessary:

Current State Future State Reference Flesh and blood Changed/glorified 1 Cor 15:50-51 Corruptible Incorruptible 1 Cor 15:53 Mortal Immortal 1 Cor 15:53 Can die Cannot die anymore Luke 20:36 Unlike Christ Like him 1 John 3:2 Image of earthy Image of heavenly 1 Cor 15:49

Romans 8:23 is decisive: "waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body." The full adoption awaited includes bodily redemption.

docs.title: huios (G5207) and teknon (G5043)
docs.text: Both "son" (huios) and "child" (teknon) are used for believers: - huios emphasizes legal status, rights, character - teknon emphasizes origin, relationship, nurture - Used interchangeably in Romans 8 (huioi in v.14; tekna in v.16-17)

docs.title: huiothesia (G5206) - Adoption
docs.text:
This word ("placing as a son") appears 5 times in NT: - Present aspect: "Spirit of adoption" received (Rom 8:15; Gal 4:5; Eph 1:5) - Future aspect: "waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body" (Rom 8:23)

The same word describes both what believers have and what they await, confirming adoption has two phases.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The NT presents a coherent two-phase doctrine of sonship:

Phase 1 - NOW (Spiritual Sonship): - Status: Believers ARE sons/children of God - Basis: Faith, receiving Christ, new birth - Evidence: Spirit of adoption (crying "Abba, Father") - Context: On earth, in mortal bodies - Nature: Spiritual, relational, legal

Phase 2 - NOT YET (Manifest Sonship): - Timing: When Christ appears / at resurrection - Event: Manifestation of the sons of God - Requirement: Bodily transformation (mortality → immortality) - Result: Like Christ, equal to angels, cannot die - Nature: Full inheritance, glorious liberty

1 John 3:2 perfectly captures both aspects:

"Beloved, NOW are we the sons of God [present reality], and it doth not yet appear what we shall be [future mystery]: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him [future certainty]."

To answer the original questions: 1. Does it refer to humans? YES 2. When - earth or heaven? BOTH (present spiritual reality + future full manifestation) 3. Physical change required? For present sonship, NO; for full manifestation, YES

docs.title: Key Observation

Every category of sexual sin known to the ancient world is addressed in the Pentateuch legislation. The categories covered include:

  2. Incest - 13 specific relationships listed (Lev 18:6-18)
  3. Homosexuality (Lev 18:22; 20:13)
  4. Bestiality (Lev 18:23; 20:15-16; Exo 22:19)
  5. Prostitution / Harlotry (Lev 19:29; Deu 23:17-18)
  6. Rape (Deu 22:25-27)
  7. Premarital sex (Deu 22:13-21; Exo 22:16-17)

  10. Levirate marriage obligations (Deu 25:5-10)
  11. Priestly marriage restrictions (Lev 21:7,13-15)
  12. Child sacrifice (associated with sexual rites, Lev 18:21; 20:2-5)

What is NOT addressed: Angel-human sexual contact.

Despite the comprehensiveness of this legislation -- covering even edge cases like Deuteronomy 25:11-12 (a woman grabbing a man's genitals during a fight) -- there is zero mention of angel-human unions, warnings about celestial beings having sexual contact with humans, or any acknowledgment that such a thing is possible.

This compilation represents every category of sexual legislation in the Pentateuch. docs.title: Analysis: Pentateuch Sexual Legislation Silence on Angel-Human Unions
The Central Question
docs.text: Moses wrote both Genesis 6:1-4 and the sexual legislation in Leviticus 18-20 and Deuteronomy 22-27. If he understood Genesis 6 as describing angel-human sexual unions -- an act so catastrophic it warranted the destruction of the entire world by flood -- why does his comprehensive sexual legislation contain zero mention of, warning about, or prohibition against angel-human sexual contact?

docs.title: Every Known Category of Sexual Sin Is Addressed
docs.text:
Moses's sexual legislation is not a brief summary. It is a detailed, systematic catalog covering every conceivable category of sexual transgression:

Category Prohibition Penalty Incest (13 types) Lev 18:6-18 Death/cut off (Lev 20:11-12,17,19-21) Adultery Lev 18:20 Death (Lev 20:10; Deu 22:22) Homosexuality Lev 18:22 Death (Lev 20:13) Bestiality Lev 18:23; Exo 22:19 Death (Lev 20:15-16; Deu 27:21) Prostitution Lev 19:29; Deu 23:17 Death for priest's daughter (Lev 21:9) Rape Deu 22:25-27 Death of the rapist Premarital sex Deu 22:13-21; Exo 22:16-17 Marriage/fine or death Sex during menstruation Lev 18:19 Cut off (Lev 20:18) Intermarriage with pagans Deu 7:3-4; Exo 34:15-16 Spiritual destruction warned Levirate marriage Deu 25:5-10 Public shaming for refusal Priestly marriage rules Lev 21:7,13-15 Restriction on who priests may marry Sexual assault (edge case) Deu 25:11-12 Amputation Angel-human unions --- ---

The legislation is exhaustive enough to include the case of a woman grabbing a man's private parts during a fight (Deu 25:11-12). Moses addressed even rare and unusual edge cases. He covered sexual contact between different species (bestiality). He addressed intermarriage across ethnic/religious boundaries. He specified 13 distinct incestuous relationships. Yet he says nothing about angel-human sexual contact.

docs.title: The Stated Intent: Comprehensiveness
docs.text:
Leviticus 18:24-30 reveals that the purpose of this legislation is to prevent Israel from committing the same sexual sins as the nations God was driving out. The text explicitly states:

  • "Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things" (18:24)
  • "All these abominations have the men of the land done" (18:27)
  • "Whosoever shall commit any of these abominations" (18:29)
  • "That ye commit not any one of these abominable customs" (18:30)

The language is deliberately comprehensive -- "any," "all," "whosoever," "any one." Moses intends this to be a thorough catalog of prohibited sexual acts.

docs.title: What the Angel View Must Claim
docs.text:
If the angel view of Genesis 6 is correct, then:

  1. Angel-human sexual unions actually occurred in history
  2. These unions were the most catastrophic sexual sin ever committed -- warranting destruction of the entire world
  3. Moses knew this because he wrote Genesis 6
  4. Yet when Moses compiled the most comprehensive sexual legislation in the Bible, he included no mention of angel-human unions

This creates an enormous problem for the angel view.

docs.title: The Silence Is Not Merely Incidental
docs.text:
The silence is not like failing to address some obscure, unlikely scenario. Under the angel view:

  • The precedent existed -- angel-human unions had actually happened
  • The consequences were known -- a worldwide flood destroyed all life
  • The danger was real -- if it happened once, preventing recurrence should be paramount
  • The author was the same person -- Moses wrote both Genesis 6 and the legislation
  • The category was addressed -- sexual legislation was the very topic at hand

An author who (a) wrote the account of the most catastrophic sexual sin in history and (b) compiled comprehensive sexual legislation would have every reason to address this specific sin. The silence is therefore not accidental -- it is significant.

docs.title: 3. What IS Addressed: Intermarriage with Pagans
Deuteronomy 7:3-4 -- The Legislative Response
docs.text:
"Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the LORD be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly."

The stated reason for prohibiting intermarriage with pagan nations is spiritual corruption -- "they will turn away thy son from following me." This is a concern about religious apostasy through marriage, not about angelic or genetic contamination.

docs.title: Exodus 34:15-16 -- The Same Warning
docs.text:
"Lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they go a whoring after their gods... And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods."

The language uses "zanah" (H2181, to go whoring) -- the same word used throughout the legislation for sexual immorality -- but applies it figuratively to idolatry. The concern is religious, not biological.

docs.title: Numbers 25:1-9 -- The Pattern in Action
docs.text:
The Baal-Peor incident shows this exact pattern: 1. Israel committed "whoredom with the daughters of Moab" (25:1) 2. The women "called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods" (25:2) 3. "The people did eat, and bowed down to their gods" (25:2) 4. "Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor" (25:3) 5. 24,000 died in the plague (25:9)

This is precisely what Deuteronomy 7:3-4 and Exodus 34:15-16 warned about. Intermarriage with pagans leads to idolatry. This is what Moses understood as the danger of improper marriages.

docs.title: The Connection to Genesis 6
docs.text:
If Genesis 6 describes intermarriage between the godly Sethite line and the ungodly Cainite line, then:

  • Genesis 6 = Godly line intermarried with ungodly line --> spiritual corruption --> universal wickedness --> flood
  • Deuteronomy 7:3-4 = Israel must not intermarry with pagans --> "they will turn away thy son" --> God's anger
  • Exodus 34:15-16 = Do not take their daughters --> "go a whoring after their gods"
  • Numbers 25 = Israel intermarried with Moab --> idolatry --> 24,000 died

The pattern is consistent: The Pentateuch addresses the same sin that Genesis 6 describes -- spiritual intermarriage leading to apostasy.

Under the Sethite view, Deuteronomy 7:3-4 IS the legislative response to the Genesis 6 pattern. This makes the Pentateuch internally coherent.

Under the angel view, there is NO legislative response to the Genesis 6 pattern, despite it being the worst sexual sin in history.

docs.title: 4. The Argumentum a Silentio -- When Is Silence Significant?
The General Rule
docs.text: Arguments from silence are normally weak. The absence of evidence is not necessarily evidence of absence.

docs.title: The Exception: When Silence Is Expected to Be Broken
docs.text:
However, an argument from silence becomes significant when:

  1. The author had reason to address the topic -- Moses wrote Genesis 6 AND the sexual legislation
  2. The category was being addressed -- comprehensive sexual legislation was the very subject
  3. The precedent was known -- the events of Genesis 6 were part of Israel's received history
  4. The consequences were catastrophic -- a worldwide flood was the result
  5. Similar categories WERE addressed -- bestiality (cross-species contact) is prohibited

All five conditions are met in this case. This is not ordinary silence -- it is the silence of an author who addressed every other category of sexual sin while writing legislation specifically intended to be comprehensive.

docs.title: Comparison with Other "Silences"
docs.text: Topic Was It Addressed? Was Silence Expected? Bestiality YES (Lev 18:23; 20:15-16) Cross-species contact addressed Homosexuality YES (Lev 18:22; 20:13) Same-sex contact addressed Intermarriage with pagans YES (Deu 7:3-4) Cross-religious marriage addressed Angel-human unions NO If it happened, YES -- especially since bestiality IS addressed

docs.title: Bestiality: Cross-Species Sexual Contact IS Prohibited
docs.text:
Leviticus 18:23 "Neither shalt thou lie with any beast to defile thyself therewith: neither shall any woman stand before a beast to lie down thereto: it [is] confusion."

The Hebrew word translated "confusion" is tebel (H8397), meaning "mixture" or "perversion." It occurs only in Leviticus 18:23 and 20:12 -- it refers specifically to an unnatural mixing.

Moses explicitly prohibits crossing the species boundary for sexual purposes. Both male and female forms of the prohibition are given. Both human and animal are to be put to death (Lev 20:15-16).

docs.title: Angel-Human Contact: An Even Greater Violation
docs.text:
If angel-human sexual unions occurred: - They would represent an even more extreme category violation than bestiality - Bestiality crosses the boundary between human and animal - Angel-human unions would cross the boundary between human and celestial/spiritual being - The consequences of bestiality are not stated to be catastrophic - The consequences of angel-human unions (per the angel view) were a worldwide flood

Yet bestiality receives explicit prohibition while angel-human contact receives nothing.

This is inexplicable under the angel view. If Moses understood Genesis 6 as describing angel-human unions, he had every reason to include an even stronger prohibition against contact with celestial beings -- at minimum, a warning. Instead, there is complete silence.

docs.title: Genesis 6:2 -- Standard Marriage Vocabulary
docs.text:
The Hebrew parser shows that Genesis 6:2 uses standard human marriage vocabulary:

  • wayyiqhu (took) -- from laqach, the normal verb for "taking" a wife
  • nashim (wives/women) -- the standard word for wives
  • bacharu (chose) -- from bachar, to choose/select

This is ordinary marriage language. Compare with Genesis 24:67 (Isaac taking Rebekah), Genesis 28:9 (Esau taking a wife), etc.

docs.title: Deuteronomy 7:3 -- The Same Vocabulary
docs.text:
Deuteronomy 7:3 uses the same "taking" vocabulary for prohibited intermarriage:

  • tithchatten (make marriages) -- from chathan, to become a son-in-law / make marriage alliance
  • lo-titten (do not give) -- from natan, your daughter to his son
  • lo-tiqqach (do not take) -- from laqach, his daughter for your son

The verb laqach (take) is used in both Genesis 6:2 and Deuteronomy 7:3 for the marriage act. Moses uses the same vocabulary to describe the Genesis 6 unions and to prohibit pagan intermarriage. This linguistic parallel supports reading Genesis 6 as human intermarriage.

docs.title: Leviticus 18:23 -- Bestiality Uses Different Category
docs.text:
The bestiality prohibition uses:

  • behemah (beast/cattle) -- the specific designation of the non-human partner
  • shekavteka (copulation) -- a specific term for the sexual act
  • tebel (confusion/mixture) -- a word for unnatural mixing

If Moses wanted to prohibit angel-human contact, he had the vocabulary to do so. He could have used "malak" (angel) or any celestial terminology and applied the same prohibition structure.

docs.title: genesis-6-sons-of-god Study
docs.text: This study established that the Sethite view is better supported by the overall biblical evidence, with the immediate context (Gen 4-5), Moses's vocabulary, God's response (Gen 6:3), and Jesus's teaching (Matt 22:30) all favoring the human interpretation.

docs.title: moses-angel-terminology Study
docs.text: This study documented that Moses consistently uses "malak" (angel/messenger) for celestial beings throughout the Pentateuch (28+ times), but never uses "bene elohim" (sons of God) for angels. If Moses meant angels in Genesis 6, he chose not to use his standard terminology.

docs.title: moses-human-god-relationship-terms Study
docs.text: This study documented that Moses calls Israel "children of the LORD your God" (Deu 14:1) and uses various other terms for humans in relationship with God. "Sons of God" (bene elohim) appears only in Genesis 6:2,4 in all of Moses's writings.

docs.title: angels-physical-form Study
docs.text: This study established that the argument "angels can eat, therefore they can reproduce" is a non sequitur. Temporary physical manifestation does not demonstrate reproductive capability. Jesus teaches that angels do not marry (Matt 22:30).

docs.title: flood-judgment-severity Study
docs.text: This study established that the flood's severity is explained by the universality of moral corruption, not by genetic contamination. The Hebrew words used (shachath, tamim, chamas, ra'ah) consistently refer to moral qualities, not genetics.

docs.title: 8. Summary of the Argument
docs.text:
1. Moses compiled the most comprehensive sexual legislation in the Bible -- addressing every known category of sexual sin, including edge cases
  2. Moses wrote Genesis 6 -- he had direct knowledge of whatever happened
  3. If the angel view is correct, Genesis 6 describes the most catastrophic sexual sin in history
  4. Yet Moses's legislation contains zero mention of angel-human sexual contact
  5. Bestiality (cross-species contact) IS prohibited -- but the allegedly more severe cross-category violation (angel-human) is not
  6. Intermarriage with pagans IS addressed -- with the stated reason being spiritual corruption, matching the Sethite reading of Genesis 6
  7. The silence is significant because it comes from the same author, in the same category of legislation, with every reason to address the topic
  8. The most natural explanation is that Moses did not understand Genesis 6 as describing angel-human unions

docs.title: Key Observations
docs.text:
1. In the Pentateuch, zanah is used for human sexual sin and figurative idolatry -- never for angel-human contact.
  2. The figurative use (idolatry as spiritual whoredom) is prominent in the intermarriage warnings (Exo 34:15-16; Deu 31:16). This confirms that Moses saw intermarriage with pagans as a spiritual/religious danger.
  3. Numbers 25:1 uses zanah for Israel's whoredom "with the daughters of Moab" -- human-to-human sexual immorality linked to pagan worship.
  4. The word is never applied to any interaction between humans and celestial beings.

docs.title: Key Observations
docs.text:
1. Toebah is Moses's strongest term of moral condemnation. It is applied to homosexuality (Lev 18:22), idolatry, and the sum of all sexual violations listed in Leviticus 18.
  2. The term covers the entire sexual legislation. Leviticus 18:26-30 applies toebah to ALL the prohibited acts collectively.
  3. If angel-human unions had occurred and caused the flood, they would be the supreme toebah -- yet the word is never applied to angel-human contact.
  4. The absence of toebah applied to angel-human contact is significant because Moses applies it to less catastrophic sexual sins (under the angel view's logic).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Reference Text Context Lev 18:23 "it [is] confusion" Bestiality prohibition Lev 20:12 "they have wrought confusion" Man lying with daughter-in-law

docs.title: Key Observations
docs.text:
1. Tebel specifically denotes unnatural mixing -- crossing a category boundary that should not be crossed.
  2. Moses coined a specialized term for cross-species sexual violation (bestiality). This shows he had the linguistic capacity to address cross-category sexual sins.
  3. If angel-human unions crossed the human-celestial boundary, Moses had the conceptual framework (tebel = unnatural mixture) and could have extended it or created an equivalent term. He did not.
  4. The Hebrew parser confirms Leviticus 18:23 uses tebel in a construct with behemah (beast/cattle), indicating Moses specifically identified the non-human party. Had he wanted to address angel-human contact, he could have similarly specified malak (angel) or any celestial term.

docs.title: Lexicon Entries
docs.text:
H2992: yabam (yaw-bam) - Part of speech: Verb - Definition: To marry a (deceased) brother's widow; perform the duty of a husband's brother - Total occurrences: 3 (Gen 38:8; Deu 25:5,7)

H2994: yebemeth (yeb-ay-meth) - Part of speech: Feminine noun - Definition: A sister-in-law; brother's wife - Total occurrences: 5 (Gen 38:8; Deu 25:7,9; Ruth 1:15)

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text:
1. Moses created specialized terminology for a very specific marriage category (levirate marriage).
  2. He legislated detailed procedures for what happens when a man refuses levirate duty (Deu 25:7-10: public shaming, shoe removal, spitting).
  3. This demonstrates Moses's legislative thoroughness. He did not just address broad categories -- he addressed very specific subcategories of marriage and created vocabulary for them.
  4. The contrast is stark: Moses legislated detailed procedures for a brother-in-law who refuses to marry his deceased brother's wife, but said nothing about the supposedly most catastrophic sexual sin in history (angel-human unions).

docs.title: Significance
docs.text:
Both Genesis 6:2 and Deuteronomy 7:3 use laqach (to take) in the context of marriage:

  • Genesis 6:2: "wayyiqhu lahem nashim" -- "and they took for themselves wives"
  • Deuteronomy 7:3: "lo-tiqqach livneka" -- "thou shalt not take [his daughter] for thy son"

This is standard human marriage vocabulary. The same verb is used for: - Abraham sending for a wife for Isaac (Gen 24:3-4) - Esau taking wives (Gen 26:34; 28:9) - Jacob's marriages (Gen 28:1-2)

The linguistic parallel between Genesis 6:2 and Deuteronomy 7:3 suggests Moses understood both passages as describing human marriages -- one describing what happened before the flood, the other legislating to prevent the same pattern.

docs.title: Hebrew Parser Output
docs.text:
Deuteronomy 7:3 uses tithchatten (Hithpael imperfect of chathan): - Root: chathan (H2859) -- to become a son-in-law; make a marriage alliance - Form: Hithpael = reflexive/reciprocal -- "make yourselves marriage-related"

This is specifically a term for intermarriage between families/peoples. It is used in the context of Israel's relationship with pagan nations. The Hithpael form emphasizes the mutual nature of the marriage alliance -- two groups joining together.

This is the same social dynamic described in Genesis 6:2: one group (sons of God) taking wives from another group (daughters of men). The vocabulary and social pattern match the human intermarriage reading.

He could have addressed angel-human unions if he understood Genesis 6 that way. He did not.

docs.title: Conclusion: Pentateuch Sexual Legislation Silence on Angel-Human Unions
Question
docs.text: Moses's sexual legislation in Leviticus 18-20 and Deuteronomy 22-27 comprehensively catalogs prohibited sexual acts: incest (Lev 18:6-18), adultery (Lev 20:10), homosexuality (Lev 18:22), bestiality (Lev 18:23; 20:15-16), prostitution (Deu 23:17-18), and more. If angel-human sexual unions actually occurred in Genesis 6 and were so catastrophic that God destroyed the entire world with a flood, why does the Pentateuch contain ZERO legislation prohibiting, warning against, or even mentioning angel-human sexual contact? What does this legislative silence imply about whether Moses understood Genesis 6 as describing angel-human unions?

docs.title: Summary Answer
docs.text:
The Pentateuch's comprehensive sexual legislation addresses every known category of sexual sin -- including 13 types of incest, adultery, homosexuality, bestiality, prostitution, rape, premarital sex, sex during menstruation, intermarriage with pagans, levirate marriage obligations, priestly marriage restrictions, and even the edge case of a woman grabbing a man's genitals during a fight (Deu 25:11-12). Yet it contains zero mention of angel-human sexual contact -- no prohibition, no warning, no penalty, no acknowledgment that such a thing is possible.

This silence is highly significant because it comes from the same author (Moses) who wrote Genesis 6:1-4, in the very category of legislation where such a prohibition would belong, and the legislation is explicitly intended to be exhaustive (Lev 18:24-30). The most natural explanation is that Moses did not understand Genesis 6 as describing angel-human unions. Instead, Moses addressed the same pattern described in Genesis 6 through his prohibition of intermarriage with pagans (Deu 7:3-4; Exo 34:15-16), which warns of spiritual corruption through marriage with the ungodly -- consistent with the Sethite interpretation.

docs.title: 1. The Comprehensive Nature of Moses's Sexual Legislation
docs.text:
Moses's legislation covers at least 12 distinct categories of sexual sin:

# Category References Penalty 1 Incest (13 specific relationships) Lev 18:6-18 Death/cut off (Lev 20:11-12,17) 2 Adultery Lev 18:20; 20:10 Death 3 Homosexuality Lev 18:22; 20:13 Death 4 Bestiality Lev 18:23; 20:15-16; Exo 22:19 Death 5 Prostitution Lev 19:29; Deu 23:17-18 Death for priest's daughter (Lev 21:9) 6 Rape Deu 22:25-27 Death 7 Premarital sex Deu 22:13-21; Exo 22:16-17 Marriage/fine or death 8 Sex during menstruation Lev 18:19; 20:18 Cut off 9 Intermarriage with pagans Deu 7:3-4; Exo 34:15-16 Spiritual destruction 10 Levirate marriage obligations Deu 25:5-10 Public shaming 11 Priestly marriage restrictions Lev 21:7,13-15 Disqualification 12 Edge case: genital assault Deu 25:11-12 Amputation -- Angel-human sexual contact NONE NONE

The legislation is detailed enough to address a woman grabbing a man's private parts during a fight, yet says nothing about the allegedly most catastrophic sexual sin in human history.

docs.title: 2. The Bestiality Comparison
docs.text:
Bestiality (Lev 18:23; 20:15-16; Exo 22:19; Deu 27:21) involves crossing the species boundary for sexual purposes. Moses explicitly prohibits this cross-category sexual contact and assigns the death penalty to both human and animal.

The Hebrew word tebel (H8397, "confusion/mixture") is used specifically for this unnatural mixing. It occurs only twice in Scripture -- both in Leviticus.

If angel-human sexual unions occurred, they would represent an even more extreme category violation: crossing the boundary not merely between species but between human and celestial being. Under the angel view, this was so catastrophic that God destroyed the entire world. Yet:

  • Bestiality receives explicit prohibition and the death penalty
  • Angel-human contact receives nothing

Moses had both the vocabulary (tebel, toebah) and the conceptual framework to address cross-category sexual violations. He did not apply them to angel-human contact.

docs.title: 3. Intermarriage with Pagans IS Addressed
docs.text:
The Pentateuch explicitly addresses intermarriage with pagan nations:

Deuteronomy 7:3-4 "Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods..."

Exodus 34:15-16 "...they go a whoring after their gods... And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods."

Numbers 25:1-9 The Baal-Peor incident: Israel's intermarriage with Moab led to idolatry and 24,000 deaths.

The stated danger of intermarriage is spiritual corruption -- "they will turn away thy son from following me." This matches the Sethite reading of Genesis 6: the godly line (sons of God/Seth) intermarried with the ungodly line (daughters of men/Cain), spiritual discernment was lost, and universal moral corruption followed.

Under the Sethite view, Deuteronomy 7:3-4 IS the legislative response to the Genesis 6 pattern, making the Pentateuch internally coherent.

docs.title: 4. The Same Marriage Vocabulary
docs.text:
The Hebrew parser confirms that Genesis 6:2 and Deuteronomy 7:3 share the same marriage vocabulary:

  • Genesis 6:2: "wayyiqhu lahem nashim" (and they took for themselves wives)
  • Deuteronomy 7:3: "lo-tiqqach livneka" (thou shalt not take for thy son)

Both use laqach (H3947, to take) -- the standard verb for human marriage. Deuteronomy 7:3 also uses chathan (H2859, to make a marriage alliance), a specifically human term for intermarriage between families or peoples. This parallel language connects the two passages as describing the same kind of act: human intermarriage.

docs.title: 5. The Argumentum a Silentio Is Valid Here
docs.text:
Arguments from silence are normally weak. However, this silence meets all criteria for significance:

Criterion Status The author had reason to address the topic Moses wrote both Genesis 6 AND the legislation The category was being addressed Comprehensive sexual legislation was the subject The precedent was known Genesis 6 events were part of Israel's history The consequences were catastrophic A worldwide flood was the result Similar categories WERE addressed Bestiality (cross-species contact) is prohibited

This is not incidental silence. It is the silence of an author who addressed every other category of sexual sin -- including an even lesser cross-category violation (bestiality) -- while compiling legislation explicitly intended to be exhaustive (Lev 18:24-30: "defile not yourselves in any of these things... all these abominations... whosoever shall commit any of these abominations").

docs.title: Under the Angel View:
docs.text:
• Moses wrote about the most catastrophic sexual sin in history (Gen 6)
  • Moses compiled comprehensive sexual legislation covering every category
  • Moses prohibited cross-species sexual contact (bestiality)
  • Moses said NOTHING about the supposedly worse cross-category violation (angel-human unions)
  • This creates an inexplicable gap in otherwise exhaustive legislation

docs.title: Under the Sethite View:
docs.text:
• Moses wrote about spiritual intermarriage between godly and ungodly lines (Gen 6)
  • Moses compiled comprehensive sexual legislation covering every category
  • Moses explicitly prohibited intermarriage with pagans (Deu 7:3-4; Exo 34:15-16)
  • Moses warned that intermarriage leads to spiritual corruption -- "they will turn away thy son"
  • Deuteronomy 7:3-4 IS the legislative response to the Genesis 6 pattern
  • The Pentateuch is internally coherent

docs.title: Final Assessment
docs.text:
The complete absence of angel-human sexual legislation in the Pentateuch is a strong indicator that Moses did not understand Genesis 6 as describing angel-human unions. This silence is significant because:

  1. Moses is the author of both texts (Genesis 6 and the sexual legislation)
  2. The legislation is explicitly comprehensive -- covering every category including edge cases
  3. Cross-species contact IS addressed (bestiality) -- but the allegedly more severe cross-category violation is not
  4. Intermarriage with pagans IS addressed -- with the stated concern being spiritual corruption, matching the Sethite reading
  5. The same marriage vocabulary connects Genesis 6:2 and Deuteronomy 7:3

The Sethite interpretation makes the Pentateuch internally consistent: Genesis 6 describes the problem (godly-ungodly intermarriage leading to universal corruption), and Deuteronomy 7:3-4 provides the legislative safeguard against the same pattern recurring. The angel interpretation leaves an inexplicable gap in otherwise exhaustive sexual legislation -- the most catastrophic sexual sin in history is never mentioned, warned against, or prohibited.

docs.title: Jesus's Interpretation: John 10:34-36
docs.text: John 10:34-35 - "Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken..."

docs.title: What Jesus Says
docs.text:
1. The "gods" were those "unto whom the word of God came"
  2. This refers to Israel receiving the Law at Sinai
  3. Jesus uses this to argue from lesser to greater (a fortiori)

docs.title: The Logic of Jesus's Argument
docs.text:
• If Scripture calls humans who received God's word "gods"
  • How much more can the Son of God claim deity?
  • This only works if the "gods" in Psalm 82 are HUMAN

If they were already divine beings, Jesus's argument collapses.

docs.title: Topic 2: "Die Like Men" - What It Means

The phrase כְּאָדָם (ke'adam) = "like/as men"

Hosea 6:7 - "But they like men have transgressed the covenant"

Israel transgressed "like men" - but they WERE men. The phrase emphasizes mortality and common human fate despite their honored position.

docs.text:
Category Passages Finding Psalm 82 context v.2-4 Judicial duties - human activity Jesus's interpretation John 10:34-35 "gods" = those who received God's word (humans) Elohim = judges Exodus 21:6; 22:8, 9, 28 Human authorities called "elohim" Parallel psalm Psalm 58:1 Same theme, calls them "sons of men" "Like men" usage Hosea 6:7; 1 Sam 4:9 Phrase used of those who ARE men "Children of God" Matt 5:9; John 1:12; Rom 8:14; Gal 3:26; 1 John 3:1-2 Applied to human believers

Every line of evidence points to HUMAN judges, not divine beings.

docs.title: The Angel View Claim
docs.text: "Psalm 82:6 refers to divine beings ('gods,' 'children of the Most High') who sinned. The phrase 'die like men' implies they weren't originally men. This supports divine beings interacting with/becoming like humans, parallel to Genesis 6."

docs.title: The Question
docs.text: Does Psalm 82 describe divine beings who will "die like men," or human judges who will die despite their honored title?

docs.title: John 10:34-36
docs.text: John 10:34-35 - "Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken..."

docs.title: Who Were the "Gods"?
docs.text:
Jesus identifies them as those "unto whom the word of God came."

This refers to: - Israel at Sinai receiving the Law - Those who received God's revelation - HUMANS who received divine communication

docs.title: Jesus's Argument Requires Human Referent
docs.text:
Jesus argues from lesser to greater: 1. Scripture calls mere humans who received God's word "gods" 2. Therefore, how can you accuse the Son of God of blasphemy for claiming deity?

This argument only works if the "gods" in Psalm 82 are HUMANS.

If they were already divine beings: - There's no "lesser to greater" logic - The argument collapses - Jesus would be comparing himself to fallen angels (problematic)

docs.title: The Verdict
docs.text: Jesus himself interprets the "gods" of Psalm 82 as humans who received God's word.

docs.title: The Activity Described
docs.text:
Verse Activity Human or Divine? v.2 "How long will ye judge unjustly?" Judicial - human judges v.2 "accept the persons of the wicked" Partiality - human corruption v.3 "Defend the poor and fatherless" Judicial duty v.3 "do justice to the afflicted and needy" Judicial duty v.4 "Deliver the poor and needy" Judicial duty v.4 "rid them out of the hand of the wicked" Judicial protection v.5 "They know not, neither will they understand" Human ignorance

Every activity is judicial - the work of human judges, not heavenly council meetings.

docs.title: The Charges
docs.text:
1. Judging unjustly (v.2)
  2. Showing partiality to the wicked (v.2)
  3. Failing to defend the poor (v.3)
  4. Failing to deliver the needy (v.4)

These are charges against corrupt human judges - the same charges made against Israel's judges throughout the OT (see Isaiah 1:23; 10:1-2; Amos 5:12).

docs.title: Part 3: "Elohim" as a Title for Human Judges
The Hebrew Evidence
docs.text: The word אֱלֹהִים (elohim) in Psalm 82:1, 6 is the same word translated: - "God" (the true God) - "gods" (false deities) - "judges" (human authorities)

docs.title: KJV Translations of Elohim as "Judges"
docs.text: Passage Hebrew KJV Translation Context Exodus 21:6 הָאֱלֹהִים "the judges" Servant brought before authorities Exodus 22:8 הָאֱלֹהִים "the judges" Theft case adjudication Exodus 22:9 הָאֱלֹהִים "the judges" Property dispute resolution Exodus 22:28 אֱלֹהִים "the gods" (margin: judges) Command not to revile authorities

docs.title: Why "Elohim" for Human Judges?
docs.text:
Judges represent God's authority on earth. They are called "elohim" because: 1. They exercise divine prerogative (judgment) 2. They represent God in civil matters 3. They are God's deputies in the administration of justice

This is an honorific title, not an ontological claim about their nature.

docs.title: Part 4: "Die Like Men" - What It Actually Means
The Hebrew Phrase
docs.text: כְּאָדָם תְּמוּתוּן (ke'adam temutun) = "like men you shall die"

docs.title: The Angel View's Interpretation
docs.text: "'Die like men' implies they weren't originally men."

docs.title: Problems with This Interpretation
docs.text:
1. Parallel usage in Hosea 6:7

Hosea 6:7 - "But they like men [כְּאָדָם, ke'adam] have transgressed the covenant"

Israel transgressed "like men" - but Israel WAS composed of men. The phrase emphasizes the manner or common human pattern, not non-human origin.

2. Parallel in Psalm 82:7b

"and fall like one of the princes"

"Fall like one of the princes" doesn't mean they weren't princes. It compares them to princes who fell (died). Similarly, "die like men" compares them to common mortals despite their exalted title.

3. The Rhetorical Force

The point is contrast: - You are called "gods" and "children of the Most High" (v.6) - Nevertheless you will die like any other mortal (v.7)

The contrast is between their exalted title and their mortal reality - not between original divine nature and punishment by mortality.

4. The Logic

If these were divine beings, why would "dying like men" be a punishment? Angels don't die. The threat of mortality only makes sense if addressed to beings who could otherwise expect to be exempt - i.e., those with the honorific title "gods" who might think themselves above ordinary mortality.

docs.title: Same Theme, Explicit Identification
docs.text:
Psalm 58:1 - "Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?"

Same elements: - Corrupt judges failing to judge righteously - Addressed as "congregation" (cf. Psalm 82:1) - Called "sons of men" (בְּנֵי אָדָם, bene adam) - explicitly HUMAN

docs.title: The Conclusion in Both Psalms
docs.text:
Psalm 82:8 Psalm 58:11 "Arise, O God, judge the earth" "he is a God that judgeth in the earth"

Both psalms conclude by appealing to God as the true Judge who will set things right - because human judges have failed.

docs.title: The Phrase
docs.text: בְּנֵי עֶלְיוֹן (bene elyon) = "children/sons of the Most High"

docs.title: Does This Require Divine Origin?
docs.text: No. Throughout Scripture, "children of..." is used for those who: - Have a special relationship with someone - Are characterized by a quality - Represent someone's authority

docs.title: Examples of "Children of God" for Humans
docs.text:
Passage Reference Who? Matthew 5:9 "shall be called the children of God" Peacemakers John 1:12 "power to become the sons of God" Believers Romans 8:14 "they are the sons of God" Those led by Spirit Galatians 3:26 "ye are all the children of God" Believers 1 John 3:1-2 "we should be called the sons of God" Believers

Humans can be called "children of God" or "children of the Most High" without being ontologically divine.

docs.title: Part 7: Why This Matters for Genesis 6
The Angel View's Use of Psalm 82
docs.text: The angel view argues: 1. Psalm 82 shows divine beings called "gods" and "children of the Most High" 2. These beings sinned and will "die like men" 3. This parallels Genesis 6 where divine "sons of God" interacted with humans

docs.title: Why This Fails
docs.text:
1. Jesus identifies the "gods" as humans who received God's word (John 10:35)
  2. The context is judicial - human judges failing in their duties
  3. "Elohim" means "judges" in multiple OT passages (Exodus 21-22)
  4. Psalm 58 (parallel) explicitly calls them "sons of men"
  5. "Die like men" emphasizes mortality despite title, not change of nature

Psalm 82 provides no support for the angel view of Genesis 6.

docs.title: What Psalm 82 Actually Describes
docs.text: Element Meaning "Gods" (elohim) Honorific title for human judges "Children of the Most High" Those with special relationship to God "Judge unjustly" Corrupt human judicial activity "Defend the poor" Judicial duty "Die like men" Mortality despite exalted title "Fall like one of the princes" Death like other fallen rulers

docs.title: The Evidence Summary
docs.text:
Evidence Finding Jesus's interpretation "gods" = those who received God's word (humans) Psalm context Judicial duties - human judges "Elohim" usage Translated "judges" in Exodus 21-22 Psalm 58 parallel Same theme, explicitly "sons of men" "Like men" phrase Used of those who ARE men (Hosea 6:7) "Children of God" Used of human believers throughout Scripture

Conclusion: Psalm 82 describes human judges who bear an honorific title but will die like any other mortal. It provides no evidence for divine beings becoming human or "dying like men."

docs.title: אֱלֹהִים (elohim) - "Gods/God/Judges"
docs.text:
Strong's H430

  • Transliteration: elohim
  • Pronunciation: el-o-heem'
  • Part of Speech: Masculine noun (plural)
  • Etymology: Plural of H433 (eloah)

Definition: Gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates/judges.

KJV Translation Frequency: - "God" - 2,346 occurrences - "god/gods" - 244 occurrences - "judge/judges" - 5 occurrences - "angels" - 1 occurrence - Other: goddess, mighty, great

Critical Finding: The KJV translators understood that elohim can mean "judges" - human authorities exercising divine prerogative.

Passages Where Elohim = Judges:

Passage Hebrew KJV Translation Exodus 21:6 הָאֱלֹהִים "the judges" Exodus 22:8 הָאֱלֹהִים "the judges" Exodus 22:9 (2x) הָאֱלֹהִים... אֱלֹהִים "the judges...the judges" Exodus 22:28 אֱלֹהִים "the gods" (margin: judges)

Psalm 82:1, 6 Usage:

v.1: "God [אֱלֹהִים] standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods [אֱלֹהִים]" v.6: "I have said, Ye [are] gods [אֱלֹהִים]"

Significance: The same word (elohim) is used for both the true God and the human judges. Context determines meaning. In Psalm 82, the context (judging unjustly, defending the poor) indicates human judges.

docs.title: עֶלְיוֹן (elyon) - "Most High"
docs.text:
Strong's H5945

  • Transliteration: elyon
  • Pronunciation: el-yone'
  • Part of Speech: Adjective/Noun
  • Etymology: From H5927 (alah - to ascend)

Definition: An elevation; as adjective: lofty; as title: the Supreme (God)

KJV Translation Frequency: - "high" - 18 occurrences - "most high" - 9 occurrences - "upper" - 8 occurrences - "higher" - 4 occurrences - "highest" - 2 occurrences - Other: above, uppermost

Psalm 82:6 Usage:

"all of you [are] children of the most High [עֶלְיוֹן, elyon]"

Significance: "Most High" (elyon) is a title for God. Being called "children of the Most High" indicates a special relationship to God - but this is used of humans throughout Scripture (see Matt 5:9; Luke 6:35; Rom 8:14).

docs.title: בֵּן (ben) - "Son/Child"
docs.text:
Strong's H1121

  • Transliteration: ben
  • Pronunciation: bane
  • Part of Speech: Masculine noun
  • Etymology: From H1129 (banah - to build)

Definition: A son; broadly: children, people, subjects; used in many relational compounds.

Common Compounds:

Hebrew Phrase Translation Meaning בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל bene Yisrael "children of Israel" בְּנֵי אָדָם bene adam "sons of men" (humans) בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים bene ha'elohim "sons of God" בְּנֵי עֶלְיוֹן bene elyon "children of the Most High"

Psalm 82:6 Usage:

"all of you [are] children [בְּנֵי, bene] of the most High"

Significance: "Children of" expresses relationship, not necessarily biological offspring. Judges are "children of the Most High" because they represent His authority.

docs.title: אָדָם (adam) - "Man/Men"
docs.text:
Strong's H120

  • Transliteration: adam
  • Pronunciation: aw-dawm'
  • Part of Speech: Masculine noun
  • Etymology: From H119 (adam - to be red)

Definition: Man, mankind, human being; used generically for humanity.

KJV Translation Frequency: - "man" - 408 occurrences - "men" - 121 occurrences - Other: person, mankind, Adam

Psalm 82:7 Usage:

"But ye shall die like men [כְּאָדָם, ke'adam]"

Key Parallel - Hosea 6:7:

"But they like men [כְּאָדָם, ke'adam] have transgressed the covenant"

Significance: The identical phrase (כְּאָדָם) is used in Hosea 6:7 of ISRAEL - who were obviously men. The phrase means "in the manner of men" or "like ordinary mortals," not "become men from a non-human state."

docs.title: שָׁפַט (shaphat) - "Judge"
docs.text:
Strong's H8199

  • Transliteration: shaphat
  • Pronunciation: shaw-fat'
  • Part of Speech: Verb
  • Etymology: A primitive root

Definition: To judge, govern, vindicate, punish; to act as judge, execute judgment.

KJV Translation Frequency: - "judge" - 119 occurrences - "judge" (noun) - 60 occurrences - Other: plead, defend, deliver

Psalm 82 Usage:

v.1: "he judgeth [יִשְׁפֹּט, yishpot] among the gods" v.2: "How long will ye judge [תִּשְׁפְּטוּ, tishpetu] unjustly" v.8: "Arise, O God, judge [שָׁפְטָה, shophtah] the earth"

Significance: The verb "judge" (shaphat) appears 3 times in this psalm. The entire context is judicial - exactly what human judges do.

docs.title: מוּת (muth) - "Die"
docs.text:
Strong's H4191

  • Transliteration: muth
  • Pronunciation: mooth
  • Part of Speech: Verb
  • Etymology: A primitive root

Definition: To die, be dead; causatively: to kill, execute.

Psalm 82:7 Usage:

"But ye shall die [תְּמוּתוּן, temutun] like men"

Significance: The verb is in the imperfect tense with the subject "you" (plural). These beings WILL die - indicating they are mortal beings who can die, not immortal beings receiving a new punishment.

docs.title: שַׂר (sar) - "Prince"
docs.text:
Strong's H8269

  • Transliteration: sar
  • Pronunciation: sar
  • Part of Speech: Masculine noun
  • Etymology: From H8323 (sarar - to have dominion)

Definition: A head person, chief, captain, ruler, prince.

Psalm 82:7 Usage:

"and fall like one of the princes [הַשָּׂרִים, hasarim]"

Significance: Princes (sarim) are human rulers. The comparison is to other human rulers who have fallen (died). This parallel confirms the "die like men" refers to ordinary human mortality.

docs.title: θεός (theos) - "God/gods"
docs.text:
Strong's G2316

  • Transliteration: theos
  • Pronunciation: theh'-os
  • Definition: A deity; the supreme Divinity; figuratively: a magistrate

John 10:34-35 Usage:

"Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods [θεοί, theoi]?" "If he called them gods [θεούς, theous], unto whom the word of God came..."

Significance: Jesus uses the Greek theos (gods) to translate the Hebrew elohim of Psalm 82:6. He identifies the "gods" as those "unto whom the word of God came" - humans who received divine revelation.

docs.title: Summary: Word Studies and Their Implications
The Key Terms in Psalm 82:6-7
docs.text: Hebrew Transliteration Meaning in Context אֱלֹהִים elohim Judges (honorific title) בְּנֵי עֶלְיוֹן bene elyon Children of the Most High (relational) כְּאָדָם ke'adam Like men (manner of death) הַשָּׂרִים hasarim The princes (parallel comparison)

docs.text: Term Evidence Conclusion אֱלֹהִים (elohim) Translated "judges" in Exodus 21-22 Can mean human authorities בְּנֵי עֶלְיוֹן (bene elyon) "Children of God" used for believers throughout Scripture Relational, not ontological כְּאָדָם (ke'adam) Used of Israel in Hosea 6:7 who WERE men Manner, not transformation שָׁפַט (shaphat) Used 3x in psalm Judicial context throughout

docs.title: Jesus's Identification (John 10:35)
docs.text: Jesus identifies the "gods" as those "unto whom the word of God came" - HUMANS who received God's revelation at Sinai.
